title: So much for sustainable packaging…
text:
Originally bought this about a year, maybe two, ago when it was a sephora online only brand. Marketed as a smaller sustainable clean beauty brand, even their 100 point sample testers were packaged in metal. Definitely on the pricier side, but I didn’t mind because all the packaging was sustainable (glass, metal, etc). Loved the formula, little bit went such a long way. Like many of their products, it took me until now to repurchase. Sad to see the packaging is like every other lip product out there in the weird crappy plastic tubes, so much for sustainability. The formula so far seems the same, I have yet to see if the application lasts overnight like the pot did. 
While I can understand changing the packaging to complete with other companies, I know the brand isn’t hurting for cash since they’re now in a decent chunk of every brick and mortar store. It would be nice to see companies that built their brand on a key component, such as sustainable packaging, actually stick with it. These changes make the customers who actually feel in love with the brand’s ethos and helped them grow feel like a slap to our faces. I rated this 4 stars because:
1. While the packaging changed to a plastic tube, the overall price is lower: pot was 0.35oz, tube is 0.5oz, both sold for $28. 
2. So far the formula feels the same to me, I purchased the tube with lot# P2406-225.
3. I really do like the rest of their products, and hope to see the company figure out a more sustainable package for the lip mask, like a redesigned version of the metal tubes they use for their sample testers.

text:
I’m in my late 30s and on a major skincare journey. My skin has changed SO MUCH from my 20s! I’ve been looking for a lightweight moisturizer to help replenish my skin, especially at night, and thought I’d give this a try.

My skin is sensitive, combination, has mild rosacea, and I have fine lines I’m desperate to iron out and plump up!

This moisturizer has an interesting texture — it feels like spreading whipped silicone on? And a little goes a very long way to fully cover my neck and face. I made the mistake once of putting too much on, and the way it just smeared around my face without absorbing at all (and I’m someone who uses several serums and essences underneath my daily moisturizer) — it was as if I was applying sunscreen that wouldn’t dry down. Eek.

After peeking at the ingredient list, it looks like Dimethicone is the culprit. It’s a silicone that helps provide slip and spread, but it definitely causes this moisturizer to “sit on top” and not fully dry down, especially since my skin is already well hydrated.

As someone who wakes up with a rather oily face to begin with, I’m not sure how I feel about this. My skin feels soft and moisturized after using it, but it doesn’t pair well with my Laneige Water Mask on top (and I love my Laneige!). It just seems to take forever to actually absorb into my skin. I think this is more of a light, breathable occlusive, but it’s not really working for me, and for the price, unfortunately, I think I’ll have to try something else.

The only issue I’ve ever had with the product was when I was keeping it in my gym bag in the winter. While I recommend using it at the gym be careful of the temperature where you store it. It was fairly cold and basically froze solid. I could scrape layers off to use, but it was TOUGH. Do not attempt to use your nails—you will break them. That being said, in the summer and spring (and some of the fall) it returned to a good temperature and as far as I can tell the formula wasn’t altered by the temperature changes.

title: Best for below-the-surface zits, but drying 3.5⭐️
text:
WHAT I LIKE:
* Easy to apply
* Adheres well; stays on overnight
* Effective most of the time (on its own or in conjunction with other pimple patches) at reducing size of deeper pimples that have not fully formed but are under-the-surface or shortening the time it takes to surface, disappear or begin to heal.
* Less messy & more effective than clay masks at addressing below-the-surface cystic-type acne (but using both in a treatment routine when  will give the best results)

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* Would be nice if these came with a few more dots for the price

FYI:
* Best for certain types of zits, at a specific stage - for me, these work best on larger, harder pimples that are below the surface - where it's not fully a noticeable bump yet but you can feel something forming under the skin
* Usually takes 2-3 uses / patches to either fully disappear or for the head to come to the surface. Usually some noticeable dryness  in the area where the acne dot was placed & around the perimeter/edges.
* TIP: To prevent/minimize the dryness that may result, (i) gently dab a little facial oil (suited to your skin type) around the outer edges of the dot AFTER it has had time to set and/or (ii) lightly apply facial oil to the area the next morning after removing the dot and cleansing your face. I found my skin was fine (acne not made worse) with jojoba oil or tamanu oil.
* I did not experience any reduction in redness where the zit in question showed signs of redness before applying the early-stage acne dot, but your mileage may vary. 
* These are nice to have on hand, especially as they are meant to be left on overnight.
* No rhyme or reason to it, but it hurt occasionally (not every use) when the microneedles were pressed against the zit.

BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ or BYE-BYE 👋🏼?:
* Despite the price, it's useful to have on hand if you experience breakouts (especially of those larger, harder, below the surface varietals) so it's a BUY 🛍️for me (on sale if possible)

title: Sheer, buildable glossy tint 💋
text:
This review is based on the set I purchased directly from the brand.

TL;DR: Lightweight, gel-like, lightly hydrating, sheer but buildable tint with a glossy finish. Feels comfortable on lips, not tacky / sticky. Color payoff on deeper shades is good on initial application & buildable to a more vibrant, bolder hue. Softer shades could do with better pigmentation on initial application but can be built up.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Lightly hydrating
* Feels comfortable on lips; not sticky or tacky
* Easy to apply/blend
* Leaves a sheer (but buildable) glossy finish
* Gives appearance of slightly more plump lips without stinging or burning
* Deeper/darker shades have good color payoff on initial application & can be buildable for a more vibrant/bolder color

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* Lighter shades could be more pigmented - takes about 3-4 layers to build up (though to be fair, my lips are more naturally pigmented to begin with)

FYI:
* Gel-like consistency
* Has a bouncy, slightly cushiony feel
* Unscented
* Slanted tip applicator
* Doesn't last as long as regular non-jelly tints
* Need to use a lot of product to amp up hydration factor
* Better color payoff on initial application with deeper shades
* Plumping is slight - you'll get a more plump appearance if you overline your lips first
* Contains skincare ingredients known for anti-aging, including peptides & vitamin E
* Can be used year round but probably better suited for warmer months if hydration is a key criteria
* There's a champagne shade (on brand site) that contains microfine shimmer that makes a lovely topper
* TIP: May want to shake tube a bit as there can be some separation if product has been sitting out for a while

BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ or BYE-BYE 👋🏼?:
* I like the sheer but buildable nature of these tints & the hydrating element, slight though it may be, so it's a BUY for me  🛍️

title: Not the best value; the products are too small
text:
I previously bought the Sunday Riley Go to Bed With Me kit and liked it a lot, so was eager to try this kit. However, even though I had a 20% discount, I did not think it was much of a value.

First, the Pink Drink is a great product but it is in a much larger container in the Go to Bed with Me kit, and, in this kit, it's just a tiny sample and is actually labeled a "free" addition on the front of the box (I'd hardly call it "free" though). So I ran out of that very fast, unfortunately. 

Next, I liked the CEO 15% Serum Brightening Serum, but it's a very small product. The jar is large but it emptied out quickly. I unscrewed the top and pulled the pastic filler pouch out and noticed that it was mainly all jar, with very little product. I managed to get every last drop out of it, but was disappointed that it ran out so fast.

Even the Ceramic Slip Cleanser was too small. Normally cleansers come with a larger size, so I was very disappointed in how fast this one ran out.

The CEO Glow Vitamin C + Turmeric Face Oil was a good product and lasted longer than the others. I also liked the CEO Afterglow Brightening Vitamin C Moisturizer, but, again, I don't think the sample size was big enough for me to really gauge whether i'd want to buy a full size product; just too small.

The Good Genes All-In-One Lactic Acid Treatment lasted a while but there are other similar products on the market and I don't see that this one is that special.

Finally, the one benefit that this Wake Up with me kit had over Go to Bed with Me was that it contains eye cream, which was missing from Go to Bed with Me. The eye cream is OK; not anything amazing and not better than the Shisedo eye cream I was using before this.

Overall, this kit is not a great value. I do like some of the products but they just empty out too quickly. I'd get it again if it's a good sale, but not at regular price.

title: The most underwhelming $89 I ever spent
text:
I bought this serum thinking it would live up to the hype, but honestly… what is this really doing? At $89, I expected to see some kind of result – smoother skin, brighter complexion, something – but it just feels like an expensive moisturizer in serum form.

Let’s Talk Ingredients:
	•	Lactic Acid – A mild exfoliant that’s great for resurfacing, but it’s pretty low in the formula. If you’re expecting deep exfoliation or glow, this isn’t it.
	•	Hyaluronic Acid – Hydrates and plumps, which is nice, but you can find this in almost every other serum (for way less).
	•	Hadasei-3 Complex – This is Tatcha’s signature blend of rice, green tea, and algae. It sounds fancy, but it’s basically antioxidants and skin-softeners. It’s nice for hydration and protection, but it’s not going to transform your skin.

Does It Work?

If you have dry or sensitive skin, this will hydrate and give you a dewy finish – but that’s about it. There’s no noticeable resurfacing, brightening, or long-term improvement. It feels like they leaned too hard into the luxury experience and forgot to make a serum that actually does something transformative.

Bottom Line:

Save your money. There are cheaper products with stronger actives that will actually give you results. If you love the Tatcha vibe, maybe you’ll enjoy the experience – but if you’re looking for performance, this isn’t it.

title: Smells great and moisturizes until it doesn't....
text:
So you know how sometimes you fall for things that are ostensibly good for you, but when you look closely, you realize they're just superficially healthy? Smoothies are a good example -- oftentimes they have vitamins and maybe even protein, but also an exorbitant amount of sugar and unnecessary additives. 

Well, Fresh's Sugar balms (this one and the others with color) are kind of like that. They glide on like a dream -- smooth and moisturizing, with the sweet scent of sugar and the faintest hint of lemon. Both the moisture and the sweetness linger for a little while before your lips start to dry out. You can reapply, but it only works if you keep reapplying...which in turn dries out your lips and sort of defeats the purpose, yes?

That said, I am a raging hypocrite because even as I write a semi-negative review about this balm, it's still a staple in my vast (also unhealthy) collection of lip balms and treatments.

Bottom line: It's a treat if -- like me -- you're kind of a sucker for marketing and love the idea of a sugar-based, sweet-smelling balm that is technically all natural. (Bad influence rec: The Fresh Sugar Watermelon balm in the pot -- which predates Harry Styles but is a fun tie-in if you're into that sort of thing -- is lovely: smells like fresh watermelon, glides on like a dream, and moisturizes until it doesn't.)

title: Vanilla + Juniper Icing
text:
Vanilla Vibezzz, full size.

I've tried this twice in the little sample form that Sephora gives out before buying the large size. I think it's wise as it isn't a scent for everyone.
Firstly, scents SMELL different ON different people because they mix with your body chemistry and heat. I always recommend trying a sample before buying a large size.
SECONDLY, this isn't a plain gourmand vanilla. A lot of people complain that this isn't giving "vanilla vibes". It's because it's not ONLY vanilla. It contains Juniper Berries- one of my favorite berries. Now, juniper berries are NOT going to be like a nice sweet blueberry. Juniper berries are used a lot in cooking, not baking.
What are juniper berries scent notes? Here ya go: Fresh & Crisp: The dominant note is a fresh, invigorating scent, like a cool breeze brushing past pine trees. Piney & Woody: It features a clear coniferous aroma, reminiscent of pine or cedarwood. Spicy & Peppery: There are warm, earthy, and sometimes peppery spicy undertones. Resinous & Sweet: You can detect a faint sweetness, a resinous quality, and subtle floral or herbal notes as the scent develops. 
Mix that with the vanilla. You get this scent.To me it smells like vanilla icing and juniper Berries- slightly peppery, slightly herbaceous. I love it for when I want a "vanilla AND" scent. If I want just a gourmand vanilla, I reach for something else.
My skin type is dry, sensitive, with eczema. I find this does not irritate my skin- but always test things out yourself. It does not absorb easily into my skin and I will stay "oily" for a while. I put it on, let it sit tight, and then go change into my clothes for the day. 
PROS: skin is shiny, looks healthy, smells good
CONS: skin acts like I put oil on it, have to be careful before touching things

title: Day 1 and Day 30 Review
text:
This product was sent to me for review, with the request that I incorporate it into my routine for 30 days. To maintain consistency, I used both an oil cleanser and a water-based cleanser when wearing makeup or sunscreen; otherwise, I used only the water-based cleanser, followed by the Mineral Milk.
My primary skin concerns are active acne and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, particularly around my t-zone, which tends to experience the most congestion and breakouts. I would self-classify my skin as mild/moderate for blemishes and inflammation so although my skin is not perfect I felt that I would likely get results relatively quickly since I only had a blemish on one side of my jaw and side of my temple on Day 1. I was hopeful that consistent use of the Mineral Milk would help clarify this area and prevent any additional acne however, over the four-week period, I didn’t notice significant changes in my skin’s condition. 

Redness and hyperpigmentation around my nose and chin remained consistent, while my forehead continued to fluctuate with bumps and acne. For active breakouts, I typically apply pimple patches to prevent picking or touching. While using the Mineral Milk, I followed this same approach, but the product’s slow dry-down time made it difficult to apply the patches immediately. I often had to wait over two hours or apply a smaller amount of product to the area before using a patch. Despite the initial dry down time being longer than many of my other products, I did not experience transfer on my pillowcase or additional oiliness on the surface of my skin in the morning that made me feel like I needed to rinse my face. Other people have commented on the scent, I also mutually agree that it has a very niche smell from the actives which does not dissipate on the skin quickly after application so if you are sensitive to fragrances it would be something to take in consideration but I accustomed to it quickly personally.

title: Vanilla + Juniper Icing
text:
Vanilla Vibezzz, full size.

I've tried this twice in the little sample form that Sephora gives out before buying the large size. I think it's wise as it isn't a scent for everyone.
Firstly, scents SMELL different ON different people because they mix with your body chemistry and heat. I always recommend trying a sample before buying a large size.
SECONDLY, this isn't a plain gourmand vanilla. A lot of people complain that this isn't giving "vanilla vibes". It's because it's not ONLY vanilla. It contains Juniper Berries- one of my favorite berries. Now, juniper berries are NOT going to be like a nice sweet blueberry. Juniper berries are used a lot in cooking, not baking.
What are juniper berries scent notes? Here ya go: Fresh & Crisp: The dominant note is a fresh, invigorating scent, like a cool breeze brushing past pine trees. Piney & Woody: It features a clear coniferous aroma, reminiscent of pine or cedarwood. Spicy & Peppery: There are warm, earthy, and sometimes peppery spicy undertones. Resinous & Sweet: You can detect a faint sweetness, a resinous quality, and subtle floral or herbal notes as the scent develops. 
Mix that with the vanilla. You get this scent.To me it smells like vanilla icing and juniper Berries- slightly peppery, slightly herbaceous. I love it for when I want a "vanilla AND" scent. If I want just a gourmand vanilla, I reach for something else.
My skin type is dry, sensitive, with eczema. I find this does not irritate my skin- but always test things out yourself. It does not absorb easily into my skin and I will stay "oily" for a while. I put it on, let it sit tight, and then go change into my clothes for the day. 
PROS: skin is shiny, looks healthy, smells good
CONS: skin acts like I put oil on it, have to be careful before touching things

title: I have been really enjoying this lip mask!
text:
I was surprised to read the negative reviews of this lip mask, because I personally really like it. I wanted to leave a review with my own thoughts, so that people could get a different perspective. To be clear, I'm not saying that those who disliked this product are wrong or that you shouldn't listen to them, I just wanted to share my own, very different experience. You can read all the reviews, both positive and negative, and decide for yourself whether this lip mask is right for you.
I have been using this lip mask pretty much every day for a couple of weeks now, and here are my thoughts:
- it does smell nice, similar to a caramel Macchiato. I will say that I get more caramel than coffee from it, but I do get a bit of both. The scent is there, but not overly strong or overpowering. 
- I personally have not noticed any plastic, perfume-y, or otherwise unpleasant taste (unlike some flavored squeeze tube lip balms I've tried). However, other reviews do mention this, so YMMV.
- more importantly to me at least, this lip mask does what it's supposed to do and leaves my lips moisturized, soft and smooth. It is very comfortable when on, and stays on all night without drying out.
- it is not sticky, gritty, or grainy (like some other lip masks I've tried).
- in addition to using it as an overnight lip mask, I find it also works great as a daytime lip balm. It's perfect for cold and dry fall/winter weather! 
- I appreciate that it comes in a tube rather than a little pot, so I don't have to use my fingers to apply it and make a mess. The applicator tip is comfortable as well.
- you can't beat the price!
- overall, I have no complaints about this product. I find it to be both effective as a lip mask, and enjoyable to use. It is one of my favorite lip masks I've tried so far. I am glad I bought it, and plan to get a few more during the sale when they're 30% off.
I hope this review was helpful!

title: Fantastic for my oily, acne-prone, dehydrated skin
text:

I used the Fenty sunscreen a few times to get the hang of it. I have pretty dry skin, and this made my skin feel greasy and oily like normal sunscreen. I doesn’t say it’s a primer, but being a makeup brand and not really knowing how to put sunscreen on after makeup, I used it first. Most of my makeup (eyeshadow, eyeliner, brows, mascara, maybe a little under eye cover and sometimes blush) did not agree with it and clumped up in places (mainly around the eyes), which then I had to wash off and start over. 

All in all, if you’re just using this for sunscreen; it’s a sunscreen. Does exactly what it says it will, and does its job well. My face has escaped burning with the product lol. As for makeup? I don’t see it meshing well with “older” (35+) skin and a makeup routine.

title: Justice for Kosas BB Burst!
text:
I was driven to write this review because this is not something I would have purchased if I was shopping online due to how poorly it’s rated. Which is a shame, because I bought it in stores and absolutely love this product. But because it has such a unique formulation, I can understand how it might catch some people off guard if they’re expecting a more traditional tinted moisturizer. Yes, when it is dispensed out of the container it looks separated…. But that’s by design and it’s because the foundation element is suspended with the skincare actives. Think of it like mixing in moisturizer to your foundation to thin it out, but prepackaged. 

My preferred method of application: I will usually work the product between my fingers/hands in order to warm it up and allow the product’s elements to meld nicely before applying directly to my face. I will occasionally fix any streakiness with a wet beauty blender or brush, but tapping the skin with my fingers works just as well in my opinion. 

For context, I was a long time fan of the MAC face and body sheer foundation and have been looking for something to replace it since it was discontinued/removed from stores. This product has a lot of the same qualities I loved about that foundation: it’s sheer but buildable, dewey but not too oily, layers beautifully with other products and does not cause breakouts on my sensitive/acne prone skin. That formula also really benefitted from being warmed in your hands before applying to the face, so maybe that’s why I like this so much :)

title: Unfortunately not a favorite of mine
text:
I recently felt that I needed a new addition to my skincare routine and I thought that a new cleanser that supported my barrier would be the best option because my skin barrier can be a bit finicky at times. I have heard great things about this cleanser from Reddit and some influencers so I decided to give it a try and found no ingredients that could potentially trigger and sort of reaction. 

For background on my skin, I have combination, acne prone, dehydrated skin that can suffer from fungal acne from time to time depending on ingredients in products. I bought and returned this cleanser twice and unfortunately both times it did not work out for my skin. The first time I used this product I suffered a reaction and my skin broke out in texture so I returned it. I believe in second chances and I was testing out different skincare products at the time so I decided to give it another go when my barrier was back to normal. The second time wasn’t any better, I broke out in texture (skin like bumps) and I developed acne. So unfortunately it didn’t work out for me :( which was a shame because I really hoped it would. 

This is just my personal skin though I just wanted to put that out there but for the overall cleanser I thought it was a decent options for those who might lean more oily. As I said before, I have combination skin, the first time I tried it I was more oily and I found it to be gentle and slightly hydrating, the second time I tried it my skin was drier and I found it to actually be more stripping than anything. However I did like the texture of the cleanser and the creamy lather. I also didn’t have problems with the product leaking. If you have skin that is dehydrated and leans dry you might want to look for another cleanser. Someone with oiler skin might enjoy this though!

title: Surely This is a Dream?
text:
I am having a difficult time believing this isn't sold out. After stewing on the price for a few months, I finally took the risk and I don't regret a thing. At 57, and some rough life choices, my skin no longer tolerates foundation. It looks horrid on me. I have taken to tints instead. 

When I first checked this product out, it looked so dark, there are so few photos it's nearly impossible to discern what it will look like when applied, and it does make some pretty bold statements without a lot of detail. In the past, Dior has been hit or miss for me, but lately, their products have left me more than a little disappointed, quality-wise. But the more I looked at other tints, the more my thoughts drifted back to DreamSkin so I decided to go with my gut. 
When it was first delivered, I swiped a bit on my face and immediately thought I had made a huge mistake. It was SO much paler on my skin than in the cushion. However, this was with a made up face at the end of the day. 
The next day, with a clean, freshly skin routined face, I dabbed it on and when I tell you it melted into my skin I mean it disappeared without a trace! So I dabbed half of my face and looked again. It looked like I hadn't put anything on so I peeled open the deep wrinkles of my skin looking for product to have settled into my wrinkles/fine lines, especially around my eyes. When I touched my skin it felt like a rose petal. What on earth is happening, I thought. So I sat back, flipped my mirror to no magnification and looked, flabbergasted.
There was my face, one half looking like normal and the other half looked like I had a filter on. What kind of voodoo is this? I don't care. Give me more!!!!
Since then, I have worn it alone, under skin tint...and yes, I did it today, over skin tint. After 30 years of not being able to wear foundation, I am now considering giving it a go. Will I? Who knows? If I want to. If not, I will just keep looking fabulously blurred and be happy as a clam. 

Thanks, Dior!

title: Incredible occlusive moisturizer
text:
I am late 20's, and have combination skin. I've used SK-II since I was in my teens, and since that time, generally have not felt a need to stray from the brand. However, they discontinued my go-to Derm Brightener moisturizer a couple of years ago. Since then, I've experimented with a lot of different moisturizers and avoided purchasing this one because of the extremely high price point. Throughout my travels with a lot of the "trendy" brands these days, such as Tatcha, Fresh, Biossance, Caudalie etc., I was still dissatisfied with my main moisturizer — Tatcha especially left me scratching my head with the texture and the fact that it made me constantly break out. Biossance, I will admit, has moisturizers that "feel" nice, but don't seem to actually improve my skin. After a year of breakouts, I caved and bought the Ultimate Revival cream. It looked like the closest SK-II product to the Derm Brightener albeit twice the price. 

And boy am I happy I made that choice! My skin started to get back to its glowing self within a few days. It's chock full of ingredients like pitera/niacinamide/zinc gluconate. Despite it being "greasy" upon first application, what I've noticed with the SK-II thick creams is that once your skin adapts to them after a couple of weeks, it loses that initial greasy feeling and instead sinks in and leaves it feeling soft and luxurious. I do have oily skin but this has not ever caused me to break out or become oilier. I only use this as a night cream due to its occlusive texture (the ingredients don't seem to confirm that it is in fact an occlusive but it definitely has that texture, might be just a heavier emollient). And for the price, I'm not even halfway through the jar and it's been four months since I purchased, so it's turning out to be decent value. A little goes a long way for this moisturizer too. 

My only possibly negative note is that it does have a distinct rosy fragrance which is pleasant enough but not really my preferred fragrance.

title: Works great but there’s a knack to using it
text: I used this spf for about a year along with a full Dr. Sturm skincare routine. It was effective, and I learned there is a knack to applying it to avoiding the pilling noted by other reviewers: your skin needs to be really hydrated. I found that when my skin was on the drier side, sun drops were really hard to apply. The product pilled and just wouldn’t sink in. But when my skin was hydrated and supple, it sunk right in and meshed beautifully with my skincare and under makeup. On the one hand, I liked realizing how much more hydrated my skin needed to be…on the other, our skin goes through phases and we doing want something as important and routine as our daily spf to be difficult to apply. Another trick when it did pill (which is something I do for any product that won’t sink in Shaun) is to spray a facial mist over the skin and then massage everything in. Works every time! There’s that hydration factor again I guess. Lastly: be aware that the regulations surrounding skincare filters are different in the US than in Europe, and the formulation for this spf is different here in the states. Sturm products are made in Germany, and my guess is they haven’t just perfected the formula for the US version. In summary, if your skin is generally well hydrated and especially if you have a Sturm routine, I think these drops are great because they can blend so beautifully and look very dewy on the skin. But there are so many amazing spf’s these days where you may get more bang for your buck. And since getting pregnant and now breastfeeding, I can’t even use this one anymore and have switched to mineral sunscreens by Tatcha and Odacité which both perform beautifully.

title: Worth it!
text:
I've never been wowed by any La Mer skincare product...until now! I used this mask every night for 3 consecutive nights until my trial sized tube finished. The first night I applied for just 10 minutes and wiped away the excess with a cotton pad, which to be honest was not that much as my skin seemed to have absorbed it all. Instantly I noticed my complexion looked more radiant and rested. For the next 2 nights I applied overnight and let it sink in and work its magic. Not only was there a brighter tone to look forward to in the morning but my skin looked more plumped and it glowed. The mask didn't extend past that point as I'd used it all up, and maybe that's a good thing as I was starting to get some small bumps (quite common for me if I use a silicone containing product on consecutive days). The breakout could also have been down to the Eucalyptus oil or Spearmint ingredients. If I was to purchase the full size I would definitely have to stick to twice per week applications at most...despite how tempting it can be to use more often when your skin ends up looking this good! Bottom line is: if your skin isn't sensitive, it's worth giving this a try. The trial size is good for at least 3 applications, could easily be stretched to four. Already a big fan of their hand cream since almost 2 decades, but this is one of the very few La Mer skincare 'face' products that I can say is actually worth the splurge.

text:
Earlier this year, a 5 hour flight followed by just 3 hours of sleep wreaked havoc on my skin: it became dried out and flaky, especially my forehead and very unusually the tip of my nose too. It was day 2 after the flight and I took one look in the mirror and one glance at my La Mer tissue mask pouch and decided there's no better time than now! The mask comes in a green foil pack and is folded up quite compactly, making it a slight task to unfold without wringing out the serum in it. It is fragranced but to my nose not in the typical 'La Mer' scent and quite subtle too. Like all La Mer products the ingredients list is very long and in this instance includes the 'miracle broth' components pretty high up on there, right after water (aqua) and a few humectants. I left it on for about 20 minutes before removing and discarding the mask, after squeezing out what remained to use on my arms/hands (I think at this price you'd be crazy not to!). Immediately after removing there was a definite glow and although not 100% gone, the flakiness did improve significantly and my skin looked a little more plumped up due to the surge of hydration. In other words it solved my flaky skin problem! I used tons of Argan oil on the previous night, straight after the flight, but it did nothing at all. Yes at over $30 USD per piece these are not cheap, but for a rare post-flight situation like mine, when nothing else worked, these did, and I would happily purchase again.

title: Day 1 and Day 30 Review
text:
This product was sent to me for review, with the request that I incorporate it into my routine for 30 days. To maintain consistency, I used both an oil cleanser and a water-based cleanser when wearing makeup or sunscreen; otherwise, I used only the water-based cleanser, followed by the Mineral Milk.
My primary skin concerns are active acne and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, particularly around my t-zone, which tends to experience the most congestion and breakouts. I would self-classify my skin as mild/moderate for blemishes and inflammation so although my skin is not perfect I felt that I would likely get results relatively quickly since I only had a blemish on one side of my jaw and side of my temple on Day 1. I was hopeful that consistent use of the Mineral Milk would help clarify this area and prevent any additional acne however, over the four-week period, I didn’t notice significant changes in my skin’s condition. 

Redness and hyperpigmentation around my nose and chin remained consistent, while my forehead continued to fluctuate with bumps and acne. For active breakouts, I typically apply pimple patches to prevent picking or touching. While using the Mineral Milk, I followed this same approach, but the product’s slow dry-down time made it difficult to apply the patches immediately. I often had to wait over two hours or apply a smaller amount of product to the area before using a patch. Despite the initial dry down time being longer than many of my other products, I did not experience transfer on my pillowcase or additional oiliness on the surface of my skin in the morning that made me feel like I needed to rinse my face. Other people have commented on the scent, I also mutually agree that it has a very niche smell from the actives which does not dissipate on the skin quickly after application so if you are sensitive to fragrances it would be something to take in consideration but I accustomed to it quickly personally.

title: Fabulous Results in 1 Minute! 🥰
text:
After trying countless exfoliating scrubs, gels, peels and peel pads from dozens of brands including dermatology formulas and much more costly skincare lines (including Dior’s Prestige), I’ve found that this is the most amazing product at this price point for my sensitive, mature, combination and aging skin (turning 50). It’s also the easiest, most economical, and effective one too. I use this 2-3x/week as directed after cleansing with my daily Capture Totale cleanser and before my routine nighttime skincare products. 1-2 minutes and I’m done! Wake up to fresh, glowing, healthy wrinkle-free skin! Incredible!

Pros: super convenient, time saving, highly efficient, gentle on my sensitive skin, and reasonably priced for this quality. To give you a point of comparison, I recently purchased the Dr. Gross Peel Pads everyone raves about. I used the Gentle, Universal, then Extra Strength gradually increasing strengths for over 2 months. I didn’t see any results with the first two and the extra strength caused a severe reaction that took a couple of weeks to heal from. It was a disaster for my skin. I also disliked having to use it daily as directed and thought the excessive packaging was stomach-churning — we have to do much better for our environment! My point is that after all of this and after spending $100/month, I can definitively tell you that this is way less expensive and far more effective without the hassle or harm to our environment. I’m back to using this wonderful product and am about to purchase another one because I know what works for me now and I’m done experimenting after so long. 

Cons: the new formula hasn’t changed results for me, but without the salicylic acid in this new formula it may be different for others. Something to consider. Also, it’s scented as all Dior products are which may be adverse or a put off to some people. I recommend trying a sample, smelling in store, and doing a skin patch test as you’d do anyway to see for yourself!

text:
One of the most effective brightening masks I've ever used, hands down. Over the years it's been slightly re-formulated and re-named multiple times. 'Brightening Derm Revival' is the latest incarnation and every bit as good as the original. Truth be told, there isn't a great deal in this tissue mask, the ingredients listing is quite basic. Just the right quantity and combination of ingredients for something exceptional. As with all tissue masks, I find these fiddly and end up cutting a line between the mouth and eye slits (both sides) so that the mask can adhere to the sides of my nose and cheeks instead of hanging over them. I leave on for up to 30 minutes and then massage in any excess into my face, neck, arms etc. Pricey - yes, but for me; very much worth it as an occasional splurge. It reduces the sallowness that my skin is prone to and leaves my overall tone brighter and more luminous. I find it works even better when used for a few consecutive nights, right before a special occasion, as the effect seems to accumulate. Been using this mask on and off for years, and keep coming back to it.

title: Justice for Kosas BB Burst!
text:
I was driven to write this review because this is not something I would have purchased if I was shopping online due to how poorly it’s rated. Which is a shame, because I bought it in stores and absolutely love this product. But because it has such a unique formulation, I can understand how it might catch some people off guard if they’re expecting a more traditional tinted moisturizer. Yes, when it is dispensed out of the container it looks separated…. But that’s by design and it’s because the foundation element is suspended with the skincare actives. Think of it like mixing in moisturizer to your foundation to thin it out, but prepackaged. 

My preferred method of application: I will usually work the product between my fingers/hands in order to warm it up and allow the product’s elements to meld nicely before applying directly to my face. I will occasionally fix any streakiness with a wet beauty blender or brush, but tapping the skin with my fingers works just as well in my opinion. 

For context, I was a long time fan of the MAC face and body sheer foundation and have been looking for something to replace it since it was discontinued/removed from stores. This product has a lot of the same qualities I loved about that foundation: it’s sheer but buildable, dewey but not too oily, layers beautifully with other products and does not cause breakouts on my sensitive/acne prone skin. That formula also really benefitted from being warmed in your hands before applying to the face, so maybe that’s why I like this so much :)

title: Instantly my favourite skincare product EVER!
text:
I originally got a sample size of this product and fell in love instantly. When that ran out, I was a little daunted by the price of the full size, but I must say, the full size is definitely worth the price given how much you get and how little product is needed with each use. 

Recently, my skin suddenly reverted back to the way it was when I was in my early teens, with lots of little whiteheads and bumps, except unlike back then, my skin now was also dry in places and was starting to show fine lines along my forehead. I used this product twice a week, and even after the first use I could see and feel a difference, the fine lines were reduced and my skin was much smoother. For an exfoliant, I was surprised that my skin didn't feel super tight or dry at all! 

My skin is relatively sensitive, but I have had almost no issues with this product. Occasionally my skin might get a little red, but I have very fair skin so it takes very little to do that. A warning: make sure when you rinse this product off, you REALLY make sure it's all rinsed off. I wasn't thorough enough once and it definitely got a little itchy in the places I missed, but once I rinsed again it was all good. 

This product can be left on for up to 10 mins, but for people with sensitive skin, I wouldn't keep it on more than 2 mins. When my skin is having a super sensitive day, I'll rinse it off pretty quickly after application. Other days, I leave it on for 5-10 mins.

I cannot recommend this product enough for pretty much everyone!

title: A great product with a bit of a learning curve
text:
This stuff is AMAZING—honestly, I think it outperforms the similar French product (the Fenty applicator is certainly more sanitary). Sometimes stubborn whiteheads or lingering blemishes just need a little help, and this delivers. It not only flattens problem areas but also creates a smooth surface that sits beautifully under makeup.

That said, there is a learning curve. For best results, apply a very thin, even layer over the area and keep your face completely still until it dries fully. Ensure the area is CLEAN first (I apply my moisturizer, then swipe back over areas to cover with micellar and hypochlorus). Rushing the application step or moving your face too soon will compromise the finish. Once it’s dry, apply makeup gently over it. If you’re too agressive with the product or makeup application, you’re probably going to have a bad time.

Pro tip: wipe off the applicator after each use and wipe again with 70% ethanol to keep it in great condition.

title: A must have until I stop breaking out
text:
TL;DR: Thin hydrocolloid patches (with salicylic acid) that suck the gunk out of pimples. A must have in the battle against blemishes. 

WHAT I LIKE: 
* Thin - thinnest pimple patches I’ve used
* Good staying power - stays in place, even overnight (but see below)
* Practically invisible - great for daytime  (but see below)
* These do an amazing job of drawing out all the gunk & pus from a zit (but see below)

* Good price - the least expensive patches, other than ones from Korean brands

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT: 
* None, really. These are my go-to pimple patches. 
* If I were to be nit picky, I’d suggest having a value sized option available; maybe double the patches. 

FYI: 
* Comes with 22 patches affixed to a sheet & packaged in a sealed pouch inside the box 
* These are meant to be used on pimples that have come to the surface, the head is visible, and there is fluid present. 
* Recommended wear time is 6-12 hours, or overnight
* As the pus is drawn out, it will show through the clear material as a white spot. May need to swap out patch throughout the day. 
* Very thin; may be helpful to use tweezers to remove the patches.
* Not waterproof; slightly water resistant. I did a test by keeping it on in the shower & having the water come down directly onto it; the edges curled up - some patches held on barely; others fell off
* Contains salicylic acid in addition to hydrocolloid (and other ingredients) so if you’re allergic / sensitive, you’ll want to use a different pimple patch. 
* I’ve tried several pimple patches like these - CosRX, Cureology, Hero, Peace Out, Peach Slices, Starface - and these are the best I’ve used. ⭐️

BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ or BYE-BYE 👋🏼?: 
* These are must haves for me. Unless something even better comes along, I’ll be BUYing these for as long as I experience breakouts. 🛍️

title: Vanilla + Juniper Icing
text:
Vanilla Vibezzz, full size.

I've tried this twice in the little sample form that Sephora gives out before buying the large size. I think it's wise as it isn't a scent for everyone.
Firstly, scents SMELL different ON different people because they mix with your body chemistry and heat. I always recommend trying a sample before buying a large size.
SECONDLY, this isn't a plain gourmand vanilla. A lot of people complain that this isn't giving "vanilla vibes". It's because it's not ONLY vanilla. It contains Juniper Berries- one of my favorite berries. Now, juniper berries are NOT going to be like a nice sweet blueberry. Juniper berries are used a lot in cooking, not baking.
What are juniper berries scent notes? Here ya go: Fresh & Crisp: The dominant note is a fresh, invigorating scent, like a cool breeze brushing past pine trees. Piney & Woody: It features a clear coniferous aroma, reminiscent of pine or cedarwood. Spicy & Peppery: There are warm, earthy, and sometimes peppery spicy undertones. Resinous & Sweet: You can detect a faint sweetness, a resinous quality, and subtle floral or herbal notes as the scent develops. 
Mix that with the vanilla. You get this scent.To me it smells like vanilla icing and juniper Berries- slightly peppery, slightly herbaceous. I love it for when I want a "vanilla AND" scent. If I want just a gourmand vanilla, I reach for something else.
My skin type is dry, sensitive, with eczema. I find this does not irritate my skin- but always test things out yourself. It does not absorb easily into my skin and I will stay "oily" for a while. I put it on, let it sit tight, and then go change into my clothes for the day. 
PROS: skin is shiny, looks healthy, smells good

title: Everything I Wanted: Sans Moisture?
text:
Ingredient-wise, this looked like everything I wanted: beta glucan, NMFs, urea, etc. Texture-wise, it’s a refreshing gel that feels nice at first with no excess shine. But minutes later, the hydration vanishes. My skin feels dry, almost as if I never applied anything. So when does “lightweight” become too lightweight? :? 

I tried all the tricks in my arsenal: layering hydrating toners, applying on damp/dry skin (even semi-damp/dry skin) misting thermal water on top. Alas, same result every time: all gel, no moisture. Since I’m beyond the return day window, I’ve been trying to use it up by adding some drops of facial oil or mixing with another moisturizer, however, that defeats the purpose of using this as a stand-alone moisturizer.

Is it awful? Not really. If you’re truly oily, this could work, especially in summer or the for those in disbelief of using a moisturizer due to having oily skin. But for most skin types, it’s too bare-bones, and could pill and/or cause breakouts from some of the lipid components.

I think The Ordinary could really improve this by reformulating. Right now, it’s basically a water gel with a sprinkle of NMFs, leaving it tacky in both texture and value. By adding more glycerin, ceramides, and NMFs, this could become a proper water gel-cream. Even 5% urea would give it a boost, and the product could then compete with more expensive brands, like SkinFix, Tatcha, or Prequel!

Overall, I had high hopes but was let down. Fingers crossed they revisit and relaunch this one with a better formula. *And yes, I’ve tried and know about The Ordinary's other moisturizers...Don’t come at me, ya’ll.

title: DO NOT BUY!
text:
I’m beyond disappointed with this product. After using this Vitamin C cream, I experienced severe irritation and dryness, especially around my eyes and I don't have particularly sensitive skin. After a few uses, the skin under my eyes became puffy, red, and inflamed. It honestly looked like Freddy Krueger skin. The swelling was so bad that my under-eye area started drooping. My eyes were literally SCREAMING: constantly watering, red, and painful to the touch.

title: My Necessity! An Underrated Product
text:
I rarely write reviews on makeup/skin products, but THIS product has earned my undying loyalty. Although this product has lasted me forever, I live in fear of it being discontinued or something and have an actual stockpile. For reference, I am in my mid-thirties and my lips are naturally large and pigmented, which WOULD be a blessing, but until this product, what usually happened is my lips would dry out quickly and they would crack to the point of bleeding. I wouldn’t be able to wear lip products because my lip texture was so uneven and anything with alcohol (lip stains) would sting the cracked, dry lips, it was a nightmare. I had tried everything, including Vaseline (everyone used to swear it would work) the Laniege (I may have spells that wrong) lip mask (which I had been assured at the time was the best), but everything disappointed.

Enter my Fenty holy grail! This is the only product that has EVER worked on my lips. The packaging is unique and LASTS FOREVER. A small amount goes a long way. The balm is soothing, it doesn’t have a taste or scent that throws me off, and you can tell it works because YOU STILL FEEL IT THE NEXT MORNING! 

I never used to be able to wear lip products, but my cracking is so much better. This product has healed my lips and makes them not only look better, but feel better. I would pay 4x the price, but the price is EXTREMELY REASONABLE FOR WHAT IS OFFERED. This product is underrated, and more people should know how important this is!

title: Liked but didn't love, def not a need.
text: So I've had this product for a little over a month and I used it consistently for about a week. I know that isn't a lot of time but i'll explain why I didn't use it everyday. I think this product works well. It definitely gives you that automatic glow once you put it on. However, the claims that this is a good overnight moisturizer are overhyped. After using this product I got temporary glow after I put it on at night. In the morning my skin was exactly like my skin was with my normal moisturizer. It wasn't super glowy or hydrated it was fine but I still had some dry spots around my eyes and near my cheek. All of this is not to say that this product isn't great. In fact I think this product works best for skin prep before makeup, a moisturizer for the winter season, and as a hand cream. It has its uses but if you're looking for an exceptional overnight moisturizer it isn't that great. It's an occasional moisturizer. Also, I have heard it does have some pore clogging ingredients. Now, while I didn't have any breakouts during the week I consistently used it other than my usual breakouts. I didn't want to take any chances hence why I only used it consistently for a week. So should you buy this product, yes and no. If you really want to try it then sure, go for it. If your in desperate need for a new moisturizer, sure buy it. If you want something for the colder months, skin prep, or hand cream by all means buy it. However, in all of these cases I think you should only get the mini size. $36 for the full size is not worth it in my opinion. Overall, I liked it but I didn't love it and honestly I could've saved $20. As someone who is easily influenced and loves a trend, you don't desperately need this product as some may claim.

title: Buyer BEWARE
text: This sunscreen gave me horrendous cystic acne that took me 3+ weeks to clear up (for reference, my dry, sensitive skin is clear at baseline). Initially I was surprised, but when I took a closer look at the ingredient list I understood why - there are MULTIPLE highly comedogenic ingredients in this sunscreen. In the product FAQs they state "Disco Block is lightweight and non-greasy, and plays well with all skin types, including breakout-prone skin." I respectfully disagree. This sunscreen made my skin look straight up like an oil slick (when applied after my usual moisturizer, with more than an hour between the two products). Many other reviewers (see Sephora) agreed. Look, I understand that no product is perfect and every product will make some people break out. But I expected a dermatologist to be able to formulate a product that is non-comedogenic and able to be used by *most* people (especially those who do not have acne at baseline). In sum - if you are even remotely acne-prone - consider giving this product a hard pass.

How to Use

Suggested Usage:
-Shake before use. 
-Gently smooth over face, eyes, and lips with a soft cotton pad, holding for a few seconds on heavily made-up areas. 
-Don‘t scrub, tug, or rub.

Please use with caution, and definitely don’t leave on without rinsing off.

title: It’s just fancy sunscreen
text:
From the start the packaging was sleek and inviting. It looks like a high quality product. I really like the refillable aspect of the sunscreen. The price however, I understand it’s for the face but these prices have gotten crazy. I wouldn’t pay full price for this product. 

The actual product was lacking guidance on how to properly put the refillable part into the dispenser. Little did I know, the bottom part of mine was twisted so when I put the refillable part in, it didn’t go down all the way and squished out product that then was wasted. 
I waited until I needed to use it again to fix that issue. The actual color of the sunscreen is pink. I didn’t notice any leaving of a tint (good thing). When going to use it again, and getting the product out of the container, it dried to a deep dark red and then the rest came out pink. I wasn’t a fan of that waste (as little as it is, the product is still extremely expensive for sunscreen, so for myself; every little bit counts). 

I used the Fenty sunscreen a few times to get the hang of it. I have pretty dry skin, and this made my skin feel greasy and oily like normal sunscreen. I doesn’t say it’s a primer, but being a makeup brand and not really knowing how to put sunscreen on after makeup, I used it first. Most of my makeup (eyeshadow, eyeliner, brows, mascara, maybe a little under eye cover and sometimes blush) did not agree with it and clumped up in places (mainly around the eyes), which then I had to wash off and start over. 

All in all, if you’re just using this for sunscreen; it’s a sunscreen. Does exactly what it says it will, and does its job well. My face has escaped burning with the product lol. As for makeup? I don’t see it meshing well with “older” (35+) skin and a makeup routine.

title: Lazy girl body care star (be careful in winter!)
text:
I have about 1/6 of the jar left so I finally feel like I can write a well-informed review.

I really like this product because it’s super easy to use, the jar is actually quite travel friendly, it’s very moisturizing, and the scent is nice and mild. It also sinks into the skin rather quickly, so by the time I’m out of the shower and drying off I don’t feel like I have a layer of grease sitting on top of my skin.

For context, one of my main reasons to purchase this was because I recently started accutane and my skin was feeling (and looking) painfully dry. I’m also very lazy/super tired in the evening. I know a multi-step body moisturizing routine would really benefit me, but some days I just want to be done once I leave the shower. This shower salve definitely hits all the marks, being super convenient and super hydrating. I love using it after shaving (I wouldn’t say it prevents ingrown hairs but I’ve found it helps) and it always leaves my skin nice and soft.

The only issue I’ve ever had with the product was when I was keeping it in my gym bag in the winter. While I recommend using it at the gym be careful of the temperature where you store it. It was fairly cold and basically froze solid. I could scrape layers off to use, but it was TOUGH. Do not attempt to use your nails—you will break them. That being said, in the summer and spring (and some of the fall) it returned to a good temperature and as far as I can tell the formula wasn’t altered by the temperature changes.

If you have dedicated body care routine I don’t know if you need this. But if you’d like to shorten/simplify or just want something easy and that provides excellent hydration for rather minimal effort, I really recommend this!

Oil and cuticle serum and hand cream religiously, multiple times per day. I kept cuticle nippers in my purse because the slightest beginning of anything would lead me to start picking at my nails and skin. Which leads to the picture below it a month later and what happened when I stopped paying constant close attention to them and let my natural habits take over. 

Now I use this at night (not even every night) and I try to use a cuticle serum or cream a couple times a day but that doesn't always happen. And then of course basic cuticle care/removal with manicures.

I don't know how it is for anti-aging, the amount of retinol is pretty low for that, but for chronic skin/cuticle/nail pickers? This is amazing.

Unfortunately, in the USA there is no legal requirement for cosmetic products, including skincare items, to have an expiration date on their labels. [I received this product for free in exchange for my honest review] When I first received the YSE Beauty - Take It Off gel-oil cleanser, I was captivated by the luxurious packaging. However, despite its eye-catching allure, the product fell short of expectations in terms of effectiveness.

The scent of the cleanser is undeniably delightful—it offers a fresh, clean aroma with light cucumber and floral tones that are soothing without being overwhelming. Unfortunately, that's where the positives ended for me. The texture of the product is quite thick, making it difficult to get out of the pump efficiently. It dispenses only a tiny amount at a time, which is frustrating when trying to remove makeup. The thick gel transforms into a slick, oily texture once applied, and I found it challenging to wash off, requiring multiple washes due to its lack of effectiveness.

The cleanser boasts an impressive array of ingredients like meadowfoam seed oil, passionfruit extract, and squalane, which are renowned for their hydrating and antioxidant-rich properties. While these ingredients promise to leave the skin feeling hydrated and supple, they unfortunately didn’t deliver these benefits for me. Despite their potential, the product left my skin feeling both oily and dry. While I'm accustomed to using two cleansers—one to remove makeup and another to clean the skin—this product made things overly complicated. It explicitly warns against using it to remove eye makeup, which is necessary as it can be quite irritating to the eye area. This means I would have to use three cleansers: one for the eyes, this one for the rest of my face, and another to remove this product’s residue. Considering its price, it seems excessive to need so many products just for effective cleansing.

text:
Let me preface that i was on a high strength prescription retinoid for about a year prior to using this product, so I am an experinced retinol user. What can I say, this is the closest ur gonna get to Retin A results in Canada OTC! I used this product on its own (with moisturizer, a bit of HA, and sunscreen of course) for about two months and it kept my raging hormonal acne at bay, kept my skin smooth, kept my skin tone relatively even, and eve. helped a bit with acne marks too (I've got richly melanated skin). Of course, this isn't the same or as effective as tret, or my holy grail, tazarotene, but its close, and really helped to manage my hormomal acne. I'm also pretty acid averse, and never use acids as they've always irritated my skin, so retinoids are my first line of defense for my highly sentitive, acne prone, oily skin. This product did not irritate my skin (coming from someone with really sensitive skin; can'teven use SA), and I only experinced mild dryness (could also be that I used it in a dry winter climate). I would defo recommend this product for acne prone skin, and don't listen to the haters, start slow, do as much as your skin can handle (I got to the point I was using it every other day to daily just fine), and MOISTURIZE. Listen, most people reach for SA and other acids, not knowing that retinoids work deeper and are much more effective (according to my personal experince and my derms opinion). Don't knock it til you try it, I found my fav acne product. And if you're reading about those who got irritated, remember, this is for experinced retinoid users only.

title: Effective Results with Consistent Use
text:
I’m 28 with dry skin, and decided to try this product because of the mixed reviews. I love an experiment, so I have carried out multiple self-assessments to evaluate its ability to diminish my deep forehead lines and skin’s appearance.

I have a fairly simple skincare routine (listed in order of application): 1) Laneige Cream Skin Toner, 2) The Ordinary Multi-Peptide Serum, 3) The Ordinary Caffeine Solution (applied around the eyes), 4) Clinique Dramatically Different Lotion+Moisturizer, and 5) a Korean sunscreen.

For this experiment, I swapped #2, the multi-peptide serum, with the GF 15% Serum. Although The Ordinary recommends using their serum twice a day, I only apply skincare in the morning, so I used it once daily. Their clinical results suggest that visible improvement can be seen after 2 weeks, with further skin firming noticeable at 4 weeks. I tested the serum over a total of 4 months, using it for one month twice, while returning to my original routine in between.

Results: Each time I started using the serum, I immediately noticed a temporary improvement in my skin's appearance. It looked brighter, smoother, and fine lines and pores were less visible. There was a slight tightening effect, but this only lasted for a few hours after application. Over time, with consistent daily use, I observed the most significant improvements in the reduction of my deep forehead lines, pores, and overall skin texture.

- Overall, I like this product and believe it delivers on its claims, but it requires consistency and time to achieve lasting results.

text: This is a moisturizer, which is much different than the vit. C serums that are easily available. There is one other skin care company I know of that makes a vit. C moisturizer, and it smells terrible. Anyway, I decided to try this--as expensive as it is, I just sucked it up to try it because I really enjoyed the cleanser. I really like this and will purchase another bottle--I did not get this for free. Anyway, the products I have purchased from this line, are really well packaged. It made me feel like I was using a special product. The only problem that I have is that you can't see when you are running low, so I am posting this review because I ran out and now I have to wait to get my new bottle. Also, I wouldn't describe Stripes as a line for "menopausal" skin but I guess that is the best way to keep things simple. I am in perimenopause, which includes the same symptoms and so does post-menopause. I guess I am being picky about language, but it could possibly turn away other potential customers from the line. Lastly, the products are scented. I actually enjoy the scents because they are not that intrusive to me and they are more herbal/wood than floral, which I am partial to anyway. Also, because I am in the Midwest, I have to layer this with another light moisturizer that I have been using for years. I apply this one first, allow it to sink in, and then apply the A*eda hydrating lotion. I stay moisturized all day even with my continued masking. My skin does not like heavy, thick anti-aging creams unless I use an active as an overnight treatment, e.g. retinol or lactic acid. It is not a miracle moisturizer, but a consistent workhorse. The formulation is really good and includes ingredients I haven't seen in a moisturizer.

title: Sheer, buildable glossy tint 💋
text:
This review is based on the set I purchased directly from the brand.

TL;DR: Lightweight, gel-like, lightly hydrating, sheer but buildable tint with a glossy finish. Feels comfortable on lips, not tacky / sticky. AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:

* Has a bouncy, slightly cushiony feel
* Unscented
* Slanted tip applicator

* There's a champagne shade (on brand site) that contains microfine shimmer that makes a lovely topper
* TIP: May want to shake tube a bit as there can be some separation if product has been sitting out for a while

BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ or BYE-BYE 👋🏼?:

title: Fantastic, affordable moisturizer!
text:
As someone who’s always on the lookout for an effective, no-nonsense moisturizer that supports the skin barrier without causing breakouts or irritation, The Ordinary's Natural Moisturizing Factors + PhytoCeramides is a standout.
Texture & Application:
This moisturizer has a lightweight yet creamy texture that absorbs easily without leaving a greasy or sticky residue. It spreads effortlessly and layers well under sunscreen or makeup, making it ideal for both day and night routines. A little goes a long way, so the tube lasts longer than you'd expect.
Key Ingredients & Benefits:
What sets this formula apart from the original NMF moisturizer is the inclusion of phyto-ceramides—plant-derived lipids that help restore and strengthen the skin barrier. Combined with amino acids, fatty acids, urea, and hyaluronic acid, it effectively locks in hydration and supports long-term skin health. The formulation is fragrance-free, making it a great choice for sensitive or reactive skin types.
Performance:
After consistent use, skin feels smoother, more resilient, and well-hydrated. It’s especially beneficial for anyone dealing with dryness, flakiness, or barrier impairment. I noticed reduced redness and less tightness in dry areas within a few days. It also pairs well with active ingredients like retinoids or acids without pilling or irritation.
Downsides:
While it's a strong performer, it may not be rich enough on its own for those with very dry skin or during harsh winter months. In that case, layering it with a facial oil or occlusive balm may be necessary. Also, those with oily skin might find it slightly too rich for daytime use in humid climates.
Final Thoughts:
This is a thoughtfully formulated, affordable moisturizer that punches above its price point. It’s a great daily hydrator for anyone looking to support their skin barrier with minimal filler ingredients.

title: Rouge Member saying GOODBYE Sephora!
text:
I’ve been a Sephora Rouge member for years, spending thousands annually and holding a Sephora credit card. That ends now.

I purchased the Patrick Ta Major Glow High Shine Body Lotion from Sephora’s website. The marketing promised a “skin-perfecting high shine” and showed comparison photos with dramatic glow versus no shine. Over a weekend, my two daughters and I tested it side-by-side with a Trader Joe’s lotion that cost a fraction of the price — and the Trader Joe’s lotion outperformed this $55 “luxury” product.

We used about 50% of the bottle during testing — enough to give it a fair shot over two days. I returned it to Sephora’s Las Vegas distribution center, expecting them to stand by their well-advertised return policy. Instead, I was told my return was denied for “excessive use” and I would not be refunded. They didn’t even offer to send the product back.

I spoke to two customer service representatives and a supervisor named Akuinda. All three refused to help, citing “policy” and making it clear there was no flexibility — not even for a Rouge member who has spent thousands with the company.

So let’s be clear: Sephora now has both my money and the product. Rouge members, take note — their return policy clearly isn’t what it’s marketed to be.

If this is how Sephora is going to treat its most loyal customers, I’ll be taking my business elsewhere, closing my Sephora credit card, and sharing my experience widely. Keeping both the refund and the product isn’t customer service — it’s theft.

title: So much for sustainable packaging…

Originally bought this about a year, maybe two, ago when it was a sephora online only brand. Like many of their products, it took me until now to repurchase. Sad to see the packaging is like every other lip product out there in the weird crappy plastic tubes, so much for sustainability. The formula so far seems the same, I have yet to see if the application lasts overnight like the pot did. 
While I can understand changing the packaging to complete with other companies, I know the brand isn’t hurting for cash since they’re now in a decent chunk of every brick and mortar store. It would be nice to see companies that built their brand on a key component, such as sustainable packaging, actually stick with it. These changes make the customers who actually feel in love with the brand’s ethos and helped them grow feel like a slap to our faces. I rated this 4 stars because:
1. While the packaging changed to a plastic tube, the overall price is lower: pot was 0.35oz, tube is 0.5oz, both sold for $28. 
2. So far the formula feels the same to me, I purchased the tube with lot# P2406-225.

title: Day 1 and Day 30 Review
text:
This product was sent to me for review, with the request that I incorporate it into my routine for 30 days. To maintain consistency, I used both an oil cleanser and a water-based cleanser when wearing makeup or sunscreen; otherwise, I used only the water-based cleanser, followed by the Mineral Milk.
My primary skin concerns are active acne and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, particularly around my t-zone, which tends to experience the most congestion and breakouts. I would self-classify my skin as mild/moderate for blemishes and inflammation so although my skin is not perfect I felt that I would likely get results relatively quickly since I only had a blemish on one side of my jaw and side of my temple on Day 1. I was hopeful that consistent use of the Mineral Milk would help clarify this area and prevent any additional acne however, over the four-week period, I didn’t notice significant changes in my skin’s condition. 

Redness and hyperpigmentation around my nose and chin remained consistent, while my forehead continued to fluctuate with bumps and acne. For active breakouts, I typically apply pimple patches to prevent picking or touching. While using the Mineral Milk, I followed this same approach, but the product’s slow dry-down time made it difficult to apply the patches immediately. I often had to wait over two hours or apply a smaller amount of product to the area before using a patch. Despite the initial dry down time being longer than many of my other products, I did not experience transfer on my pillowcase or additional oiliness on the surface of my skin in the morning that made me feel like I needed to rinse my face. Other people have commented on the scent, I also mutually agree that it has a very niche smell from the actives which does not dissipate on the skin quickly after application so if you are sensitive to fragrances it would be something to take in consideration but I accustomed to it quickly personally.

One reviewer mentioned bottles breaking. I’m not sure what they’re doing to their bottles but I have never had one break in 6+ years :)

text:

- The tint completely blends in without being too dark or leaving a white cast. That said, I'm super fair so YMMV
- No pilling over skincare or under makeup
- Silicone-free
- It has a slightly tacky finish that my foundation (also silicone free) really grips on to and it stays in place throughout the day, so this seems to double as a primer for me

- NO BREAKOUTS!!!!

Cons:
- It's only SPF 30, and my biggest complaint is that it isn't higher. That said, you can use enough product to reach that level of protection and it all absorbs beautifully

title: Vanilla + Juniper Icing
text:
Vanilla Vibezzz, full size.

I've tried this twice in the little sample form that Sephora gives out before buying the large size. I think it's wise as it isn't a scent for everyone.
Firstly, scents SMELL different ON different people because they mix with your body chemistry and heat. I always recommend trying a sample before buying a large size.
SECONDLY, this isn't a plain gourmand vanilla. A lot of people complain that this isn't giving "vanilla vibes". It's because it's not ONLY vanilla. It contains Juniper Berries- one of my favorite berries. Now, juniper berries are NOT going to be like a nice sweet blueberry. Juniper berries are used a lot in cooking, not baking.
What are juniper berries scent notes? Here ya go: Fresh & Crisp: The dominant note is a fresh, invigorating scent, like a cool breeze brushing past pine trees. Piney & Woody: It features a clear coniferous aroma, reminiscent of pine or cedarwood. Spicy & Peppery: There are warm, earthy, and sometimes peppery spicy undertones. Resinous & Sweet: You can detect a faint sweetness, a resinous quality, and subtle floral or herbal notes as the scent develops. 
Mix that with the vanilla. You get this scent.To me it smells like vanilla icing and juniper Berries- slightly peppery, slightly herbaceous. I love it for when I want a "vanilla AND" scent. If I want just a gourmand vanilla, I reach for something else.
My skin type is dry, sensitive, with eczema. I find this does not irritate my skin- but always test things out yourself. It does not absorb easily into my skin and I will stay "oily" for a while. I put it on, let it sit tight, and then go change into my clothes for the day. 
PROS: skin is shiny, looks healthy, smells good
CONS: skin acts like I put oil on it, have to be careful before touching things

title: It's a love hate, but love mostly wins.
text:
I have very dry lips that become extremely dry in colder months.  I'm on a mission to try all lip oils and balms to find the most soothing for me.  This is not in contention for the best, but it is definitely a good option.

The pros - it soothes and hydrates my dry lips.  The effect was almost immediate in softening parts of my lips that felt ready to crack and bleed.  The applicator is plush to make application gentle on sore lips and it adds the faintest hint of red.

The cons - it feels more like a jelly going on than an oil.  It's thick and spreads quickly beyond the lip line.  That's okay, mostly, for me since hydration matters more than looks, but it feels messy.  Probably looks it too, which is why I immediately put this on my nightstand to go with my lip masks.  It doesn't have a taste, but I feel like there is a scent to it that I don't love.  The jelly texture does melt to more of an oil feel, but even as dry as my lips are, it seems to take quite a while to absorb and I'm not the biggest fan of the texture.  My lips aren't sticky, they're slick.  I honestly wiped it off the first time I tried it when the feeling of something oily on my lips persisted for more than 10 minutes.  The first wear was during the day, so I didn't like it, but I tolerate that kind of thing better at night for bed.  I've used this under lip masks after giving it several minutes to settle before layering more on and I've used it on top of lip balms I sometimes apply before bed.  Neither method seems to change the texture on the lip, but both do help soothe and soften my lips at the end of the day to give me a fresh start in the morning.

The price is overall good in comparison to others I've tried with similar effect, so I put it in my 4 star grouping despite the cons.  It also gets a bump in tier for the soothing quality that helped me after mistakingly putting on a plumping gloss that had my lips burning.  This helped with that too.

title: Amazing product.
text:
I’ve never written a review before, but I truly felt compelled to share my experience in hopes that it helps other women like me. I'm 52 years old and from Andhra Pradesh, South India. For years, I’ve struggled with pigmentation and dark spots around my mouth and on the sides of my face due to hyperthyroidism.
I even went through laser treatment once. It worked for a while, but the spots came back after three years. My doctors recommended either repeating the laser or using daily brightening pads—but with my very sensitive skin, I wasn’t comfortable with those options. Nothing really seemed to work for me.
Then one day, I came across a reel on Facebook about KATINI SKIN Celestial Nightly Repair Oil-Serum, and I decided to give it a try. I started using it on June 11, 2025, and now, after two months, I can honestly say I’m amazed by the results. The only thing I personally found a bit difficult was the strong fragrance—as soon as I apply it, I tend to sneeze a lot because of the smell. But apart from that, the product has been incredibly effective and gentle on my skin.
About 50% of my pigmentation has cleared, and my skin feels so much smoother, calmer, and has a healthy glow. I haven’t had any itching, pimples, or breakouts, which is a huge relief. I was so impressed that I even started applying it to my elbows and knees—and those dark areas have started clearing up too!
This serum has truly made a difference not just in my skin, but in my confidence. I’m so thankful I found it. If you're dealing with similar issues, especially with very sensitive skin, I would highly recommend giving it a try. It worked wonders for me, maybe for you too.

title: I LOVE THIS PRODUCT!
text:
This is definitely a, "I never write reviews, but I had to for this one" review. 

I'd been wanting to add a retinol into my skincare routine but I was nervous to try one because I have such sensitive skin. I decided to go the plant-based route and used a whole bottle of the Herbivore Bakuchiol Smoothing Serum but never really noticed any difference. Then I came across this and I liked that it was a phyto-retinol but also a 3 in1 situation. It had a lot of good reviews but a lot were from gifted product which sometimes makes me question if the hype is real but i'm here to say the hype IS REAL. I know it sounds crazy but literally the next day after using this my skin felt smoother, tighter and I even noticed some of my fine lines were gone.
