title: Day 1 and Day 30 Review
text:
This product was sent to me for review, with the request that I incorporate it into my routine for 30 days. To maintain consistency, I used both an oil cleanser and a water-based cleanser when wearing makeup or sunscreen; otherwise, I used only the water-based cleanser, followed by the Mineral Milk.
My primary skin concerns are active acne and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, particularly around my t-zone, which tends to experience the most congestion and breakouts. I would self-classify my skin as mild/moderate for blemishes and inflammation so although my skin is not perfect I felt that I would likely get results relatively quickly since I only had a blemish on one side of my jaw and side of my temple on Day 1. I was hopeful that consistent use of the Mineral Milk would help clarify this area and prevent any additional acne however, over the four-week period, I didn’t notice significant changes in my skin’s condition. 

Redness and hyperpigmentation around my nose and chin remained consistent, while my forehead continued to fluctuate with bumps and acne. For active breakouts, I typically apply pimple patches to prevent picking or touching. While using the Mineral Milk, I followed this same approach, but the product’s slow dry-down time made it difficult to apply the patches immediately. I often had to wait over two hours or apply a smaller amount of product to the area before using a patch. Despite the initial dry down time being longer than many of my other products, I did not experience transfer on my pillowcase or additional oiliness on the surface of my skin in the morning that made me feel like I needed to rinse my face. Other people have commented on the scent, I also mutually agree that it has a very niche smell from the actives which does not dissipate on the skin quickly after application so if you are sensitive to fragrances it would be something to take in consideration but I accustomed to it quickly personally.

Originally bought this about a year, maybe two, ago when it was a sephora online only brand. While I can understand changing the packaging to complete with other companies, I know the brand isn’t hurting for cash since they’re now in a decent chunk of every brick and mortar store. It would be nice to see companies that built their brand on a key component, such as sustainable packaging, actually stick with it. These changes make the customers who actually feel in love with the brand’s ethos and helped them grow feel like a slap to our faces. I rated this 4 stars because:

title: Luxe SPF with a smoothe, creamy consistency
text:
TL;DR: Lightweight, mineral sunscreen with a golden yellow tint & a smooth, creamy consistency that feels lightly hydrating and moisturizing on the skin. Depending on skin type & tone, it adds a healthy glow and warmth to the complexion.

Best suited for normal or dry skin types, and possibly combination skin. Those with very oily skin may find the glow to be too much.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Lightweight, silky, soft cream consistency - it literally glides onto the skin
* Mineral UV filters - 20% zinc oxide (the tint to this keeps it from leaving a white cast)
* Contains vitamin C, which gives a soft, natural glow to the skin
* Contains hydrating, moisturizing, & soothing ingredients
* Diminishes appearance of redness & dark spots - it won’t make them completely disappear but just one layer will make them less visible
* Wears well under makeup, no pilling
* Expiration date is listed on back of tube

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* Would be nice if it was packaged in such a way that the user can see how much product remains
* Would love to see a mini version be made available, or even in a discovery set. Or, alternatively, for a deluxe size sample as a promo gwp. It's an expensive sunscreen & being able to try it out beforehand would be great.

FYI:
* Has a soft, fresh, citrusy scent, not overpowering.
* Feels lightly moisturizing & hydrating on my skin but not so much that I would skip my moisturizer
* The tint on this is probably best suited for light-to-medium warm tones
* The glow from this SPF may be too much for those with oily to very oily skin
* Dispenses smoothly from the tube (took 17 pumps on 1st use to get the product to come out)
* Pricey for SPF. I picked it up during Sephora's 50% off sale on certain products.

BUY, BUY, BUY🛍️ or BYE-BYE👋🏼?:

title: Fantastic for my oily, acne-prone, dehydrated skin
text:
I have oily, dehydrated, acne prone skin and finding an SPF that doesn't exacerbate at least one of those issues has been challenging. I've been using Star Seed for a week and it's really working for me so I hope this review is helpful for people whose skin is as finicky as mine!

Pros:
- Not dewy or greasy, and doesn't get oily throughout the day
- Absorbs fully into the skin without leaving a film
- Dries down to a lovely velvet-matte finish without drying out my skin
- The tint completely blends in without being too dark or leaving a white cast. That said, I'm super fair so YMMV
- No pilling over skincare or under makeup
- Silicone-free
- It has a slightly tacky finish that my foundation (also silicone free) really grips on to and it stays in place throughout the day, so this seems to double as a primer for me
- It's not hydrating enough by itself at the moment, but I can see how I might be able to skip moisturizer if I use this during the summer
- NO BREAKOUTS!!!!

Cons:
- It's only SPF 30, and my biggest complaint is that it isn't higher. That said, you can use enough product to reach that level of protection and it all absorbs beautifully
- Contains added fragrance. My skin isn't sensitive to fragrance and the scent isn't strong enough to bother me so that's not a dealbreaker for me
- It has butyloctyl salicylate so it's technically not 100% mineral, but again, not a dealbreaker for me personally

I may end up reaching for a product with a higher SPF come summer, but for now it's fantastic and I am SO glad I found it!

title: Vanilla + Juniper Icing
text:
Vanilla Vibezzz, full size.

I've tried this twice in the little sample form that Sephora gives out before buying the large size. I think it's wise as it isn't a scent for everyone.
Firstly, scents SMELL different ON different people because they mix with your body chemistry and heat. I always recommend trying a sample before buying a large size.
SECONDLY, this isn't a plain gourmand vanilla. A lot of people complain that this isn't giving "vanilla vibes". It's because it's not ONLY vanilla. It contains Juniper Berries- one of my favorite berries. Now, juniper berries are NOT going to be like a nice sweet blueberry. Juniper berries are used a lot in cooking, not baking.
What are juniper berries scent notes? Here ya go: Fresh & Crisp: The dominant note is a fresh, invigorating scent, like a cool breeze brushing past pine trees. Piney & Woody: It features a clear coniferous aroma, reminiscent of pine or cedarwood. Spicy & Peppery: There are warm, earthy, and sometimes peppery spicy undertones. Resinous & Sweet: You can detect a faint sweetness, a resinous quality, and subtle floral or herbal notes as the scent develops. 
Mix that with the vanilla. You get this scent.To me it smells like vanilla icing and juniper Berries- slightly peppery, slightly herbaceous. I love it for when I want a "vanilla AND" scent. If I want just a gourmand vanilla, I reach for something else.
My skin type is dry, sensitive, with eczema. I find this does not irritate my skin- but always test things out yourself. It does not absorb easily into my skin and I will stay "oily" for a while. I put it on, let it sit tight, and then go change into my clothes for the day. 
PROS: skin is shiny, looks healthy, smells good
CONS: skin acts like I put oil on it, have to be careful before touching things

title: Vanilla + Juniper Icing
text:
Vanilla Vibezzz, full size.

I've tried this twice in the little sample form that Sephora gives out before buying the large size. I think it's wise as it isn't a scent for everyone.
Firstly, scents SMELL different ON different people because they mix with your body chemistry and heat. I always recommend trying a sample before buying a large size.
SECONDLY, this isn't a plain gourmand vanilla. A lot of people complain that this isn't giving "vanilla vibes". It's because it's not ONLY vanilla. It contains Juniper Berries- one of my favorite berries. Now, juniper berries are NOT going to be like a nice sweet blueberry. Juniper berries are used a lot in cooking, not baking.
What are juniper berries scent notes? Here ya go: Fresh & Crisp: The dominant note is a fresh, invigorating scent, like a cool breeze brushing past pine trees. Piney & Woody: It features a clear coniferous aroma, reminiscent of pine or cedarwood. Spicy & Peppery: There are warm, earthy, and sometimes peppery spicy undertones. Resinous & Sweet: You can detect a faint sweetness, a resinous quality, and subtle floral or herbal notes as the scent develops. 
Mix that with the vanilla. You get this scent.To me it smells like vanilla icing and juniper Berries- slightly peppery, slightly herbaceous. I love it for when I want a "vanilla AND" scent. If I want just a gourmand vanilla, I reach for something else.
My skin type is dry, sensitive, with eczema. I find this does not irritate my skin- but always test things out yourself. It does not absorb easily into my skin and I will stay "oily" for a while. I put it on, let it sit tight, and then go change into my clothes for the day. 
PROS: skin is shiny, looks healthy, smells good
CONS: skin acts like I put oil on it, have to be careful before touching things

title: Lovely cream but the jar is terrible
text: After going through a jar of this cream, I can tell you that it’s great! It moisturizes, isn’t greasy, sinks in quickly and I don’t feel like it’s clogging up my pores. It’s very lightweight and a great choice for warmer weather. Do I see dramatic results with it? Are my pores suddenly all cleared up? No. But I honestly wasn’t expecting a miracle product. I just wanted a product to go with the Retin A that I’ve been using. And it does just that. It moisturizes while not causing acne flare ups. I bought a second jar and plan to keep on using it. Couple of issues though. One is that because it has acids in it, your skin may actually dry out when you first start using it. This eventually evens out though. Second issue is the packaging. The jar shape is awful. The jar is so wide that it requires you to use your finger to swirl along the edge to dig out product. It’s a lovely jar but I’d love a straight edged jar instead. title: Lazy girl body care star (be careful in winter!)
text:
I have about 1/6 of the jar left so I finally feel like I can write a well-informed review.

I really like this product because it’s super easy to use, the jar is actually quite travel friendly, it’s very moisturizing, and the scent is nice and mild. It also sinks into the skin rather quickly, so by the time I’m out of the shower and drying off I don’t feel like I have a layer of grease sitting on top of my skin.

For context, one of my main reasons to purchase this was because I recently started accutane and my skin was feeling (and looking) painfully dry. I’m also very lazy/super tired in the evening. I know a multi-step body moisturizing routine would really benefit me, but some days I just want to be done once I leave the shower. This shower salve definitely hits all the marks, being super convenient and super hydrating. C moisturizer, and it smells terrible. Anyway, I decided to try this--as expensive as it is, I just sucked it up to try it because I really enjoyed the cleanser. Also, I wouldn't describe Stripes as a line for "menopausal" skin but I guess that is the best way to keep things simple. I am in perimenopause, which includes the same symptoms and so does post-menopause. I guess I am being picky about language, but it could possibly turn away other potential customers from the line. Lastly, the products are scented. I actually enjoy the scents because they are not that intrusive to me and they are more herbal/wood than floral, which I am partial to anyway. Also, because I am in the Midwest, I have to layer this with another light moisturizer that I have been using for years. I apply this one first, allow it to sink in, and then apply the A*eda hydrating lotion. I stay moisturized all day even with my continued masking. My skin does not like heavy, thick anti-aging creams unless I use an active as an overnight treatment, e.g. retinol or lactic acid. It is not a miracle moisturizer, but a consistent workhorse. title: Just sits on top of my skin and smears around.
text:
I’m in my late 30s and on a major skincare journey. My skin has changed SO MUCH from my 20s! I’ve been looking for a lightweight moisturizer to help replenish my skin, especially at night, and thought I’d give this a try.

My skin is sensitive, combination, has mild rosacea, and I have fine lines I’m desperate to iron out and plump up!

This moisturizer has an interesting texture — it feels like spreading whipped silicone on? And a little goes a very long way to fully cover my neck and face. I made the mistake once of putting too much on, and the way it just smeared around my face without absorbing at all (and I’m someone who uses several serums and essences underneath my daily moisturizer) — it was as if I was applying sunscreen that wouldn’t dry down. Eek.

After peeking at the ingredient list, it looks like Dimethicone is the culprit. It’s a silicone that helps provide slip and spread, but it definitely causes this moisturizer to “sit on top” and not fully dry down, especially since my skin is already well hydrated.

As someone who wakes up with a rather oily face to begin with, I’m not sure how I feel about this. My skin feels soft and moisturized after using it, but it doesn’t pair well with my Laneige Water Mask on top (and I love my Laneige!). It just seems to take forever to actually absorb into my skin. I think this is more of a light, breathable occlusive, but it’s not really working for me, and for the price, unfortunately, I think I’ll have to try something else.

title: Actually a pretty good product, worth buying imo
text:
I was hesitant to buy this product initially despite it being on sale at the time because of all of the reviews that said it either didn't do anything or that it was impossible to actually get it on the skin because it was so stiff. But I caved and got it anyway because I have tried everything to get rid of my dark circles and so far nothing I've used has made a considerable difference so I figured why not. I didn't expect much from this product initially but after using it for a couple of days, twice a day, once in the morning and once at night, I already notice a considerable difference in the appearance of my dark circles. I've always had really really dark ones that stuck out like a sore thumb on my pretty light skin but now, on my right eye they are pretty much gone already and on my left eye they are just barely visible. Not sure why it affected both eyes differently but it's still certainly an improvement from how it was before. 

Despite what other reviews say, the stick glides on super easily for me and provides a nice light glow because of the shimmer inside of it. This glow does stand out, but it does not overpower your face, at least for me. I'm not sure how it would look on other skin types/skin colors. This product also did not have an odd texture for me, unlike what others are saying. It was completely smooth after application and was not super greasy at all. One thing I do agree with others on though is that it does have a very distinct smell. It does not bother me as I have gotten used to it but I can definitely see how it might bother those who have a sensitive nose and how that could be a downside. That being said though, upon doing some research, a distinct smell like the one in this product is normal for serums and products that contain vitamin C. Other than this though, all in all, the product is amazing and definitely works. It is absolutely worth it, even at full price (I got it for half off I believe).

title: Good Quality; However, There Are Still Issues
text:
Let me start with the Positive: Product feels refreshingly soothing, especially on days when skin feels taut, looks dry, or simply needs pampering.
Now for the other issues, and I have 3:
1. Product category - This is marketed as a treatment lotion. The term "lotion" is rather misleading because of its watery consistency. In my opinion, a lotion is a tad more viscous.
I also hesitate to call this a "toner" because it is not indicated for wiping off residual impurities after cleansing. I'm therefore more inclined to call this an "essence," primarily because of the botanical extracts included in the formula, though they may not be as concentrated as a those found in a "serum."
2. Packaging - I received this as part of a travel kit in a 50mL bottle with a screw cap.  Being watery in consistency, it is difficult to dispense the right amount without spilling and wasting its precious contents. I have since decanted into a bottle with a flip-top cap.
3. Price point - Due to its high price tag, I generally reserve the use of this to personal spa days. I am currently trying lesser expensive products from The Inkey List and The Ordinary. The Drugstore is not off-limits in my quest for affordable, ethically sourced, yet highly effective skin care products.

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] Ok this formula ACTUALLY impressed me! I’m late 30s with combination skin and am blessed with both active acne and wrinkles (why??) Not this formula! She’s easy and seems to wash off well. And I have tested for about three weeks now before writing this review.

I can’t detect much of a scent, and the texture is very watery. (Which I prefer, because combo skin doesn’t do well with thick products.) So you’ll need to work it into your skin as soon as you apply it. I love that the applicator has a precision tip, cause this allows me to almost draw it on my face and then massage it in. 

I am Mediterranean with an olive tone to my skin, and I do not see any white cast. This has a slightly dewy finish to it, which I prefer to finish off with setting powder, because my skin is still naturally slightly oily. And this is 50 SPF too!

Nicely done, Paula’s choice! I think I might re-purchase this when it runs out.

title: It’s just fancy sunscreen
text:
From the start the packaging was sleek and inviting. It looks like a high quality product. I really like the refillable aspect of the sunscreen. The price however, I understand it’s for the face but these prices have gotten crazy. I wouldn’t pay full price for this product. 

The actual product was lacking guidance on how to properly put the refillable part into the dispenser. Little did I know, the bottom part of mine was twisted so when I put the refillable part in, it didn’t go down all the way and squished out product that then was wasted. 
I waited until I needed to use it again to fix that issue. The actual color of the sunscreen is pink. I didn’t notice any leaving of a tint (good thing). When going to use it again, and getting the product out of the container, it dried to a deep dark red and then the rest came out pink. I wasn’t a fan of that waste (as little as it is, the product is still extremely expensive for sunscreen, so for myself; every little bit counts). 

I used the Fenty sunscreen a few times to get the hang of it. I have pretty dry skin, and this made my skin feel greasy and oily like normal sunscreen. I doesn’t say it’s a primer, but being a makeup brand and not really knowing how to put sunscreen on after makeup, I used it first. Most of my makeup (eyeshadow, eyeliner, brows, mascara, maybe a little under eye cover and sometimes blush) did not agree with it and clumped up in places (mainly around the eyes), which then I had to wash off and start over. 

All in all, if you’re just using this for sunscreen; it’s a sunscreen. Does exactly what it says it will, and does its job well. My face has escaped burning with the product lol. As for makeup? I don’t see it meshing well with “older” (35+) skin and a makeup routine.

text:
WHAT I LIKE:

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* Would be nice if these came with a few more dots for the price

FYI:
* Best for certain types of zits, at a specific stage - for me, these work best on larger, harder pimples that are below the surface - where it's not fully a noticeable bump yet but you can feel something forming under the skin
* Usually takes 2-3 uses / patches to either fully disappear or for the head to come to the surface. Usually some noticeable dryness  in the area where the acne dot was placed & around the perimeter/edges.
* TIP: To prevent/minimize the dryness that may result, (i) gently dab a little facial oil (suited to your skin type) around the outer edges of the dot AFTER it has had time to set and/or (ii) lightly apply facial oil to the area the next morning after removing the dot and cleansing your face. I found my skin was fine (acne not made worse) with jojoba oil or tamanu oil.
* I did not experience any reduction in redness where the zit in question showed signs of redness before applying the early-stage acne dot, but your mileage may vary. 
* These are nice to have on hand, especially as they are meant to be left on overnight.
* No rhyme or reason to it, but it hurt occasionally (not every use) when the microneedles were pressed against the zit.

* Despite the price, it's useful to have on hand if you experience breakouts (especially of those larger, harder, below the surface varietals) so it's a BUY 🛍️for me (on sale if possible)

title: A great product with a bit of a learning curve
text:
This stuff is AMAZING—honestly, I think it outperforms the similar French product (the Fenty applicator is certainly more sanitary). Sometimes stubborn whiteheads or lingering blemishes just need a little help, and this delivers. It not only flattens problem areas but also creates a smooth surface that sits beautifully under makeup.

That said, there is a learning curve. For best results, apply a very thin, even layer over the area and keep your face completely still until it dries fully. Ensure the area is CLEAN first (I apply my moisturizer, then swipe back over areas to cover with micellar and hypochlorus). Rushing the application step or moving your face too soon will compromise the finish. Once it’s dry, apply makeup gently over it. If you’re too agressive with the product or makeup application, you’re probably going to have a bad time.

Pro tip: wipe off the applicator after each use and wipe again with 70% ethanol to keep it in great condition.

I think this product works well. It definitely gives you that automatic glow once you put it on. However, the claims that this is a good overnight moisturizer are overhyped. Now, while I didn't have any breakouts during the week I consistently used it other than my usual breakouts. I didn't want to take any chances hence why I only used it consistently for a week. So should you buy this product, yes and no. If you really want to try it then sure, go for it. If your in desperate need for a new moisturizer, sure buy it. If you want something for the colder months, skin prep, or hand cream by all means buy it. However, in all of these cases I think you should only get the mini size. $36 for the full size is not worth it in my opinion. Overall, I liked it but I didn't love it and honestly I could've saved $20. As someone who is easily influenced and loves a trend, you don't desperately need this product as some may claim.

title: Slightly comedogenic, broke me out

I understand that skincare is highly individual and that this product may work beautifully for some, but I wish I had done more research before trying it. I also found the absorption to be uneven, and it didn’t seal in moisture effectively, which led to breakouts after just a few days.

For those with similar concerns, I’d recommend opting for a non-comedogenic, more occlusive product like tallow (I use grass-fed & finished suet, and it has cleared my skin completely) or jojoba oil. Both have worked well for me when applied after essence or moisturizer and have never caused breakouts.

As I have combination skin, I look for cleansers that *actually* cleanse without stripping my skin and leaving a tight, dry feeling after they are rinsed off. This one definitely fits the bill. title: Throwing in the trash!
text:
I love lactic acid. I have used lactic acid regularly in my skincare routine for the better part of the last decade. I have used many different formulations, including inexpensive, barebones serums, and pricier serums with other included actives, like this one. This serum, however, is by far the worst lactic acid serum I have ever used. I purchased this in May, at the urging of a trusted fellow skincare fanatic after my favorite lactic acid serum was discontinued. I was so excited to try it...and it did absolutely nothing. My skin usually reacts immediately to lactic acid, with increased brightness in the short term, and smoother texture in the long term. I observed no discernible difference in my skin after a solid 6 weeks of regular use. I continued to use it, however, because it is NOT cheap, and I wanted to give it more time to work (again, usually unnecessary with lactic acid, but I was hopeful).  To date, all this serum has done is BURN me. My forehead and cheek are currently dark and scaly, as if I have had a chemical peel. This is the second time this has happened while using this serum. It has never happened to me with any other lactic acid serum I've used. I also want to point out that I have used moisturizing creams with PHA and never had this result from any of them. I wouldn't be so upset about the peeling if the new skin underneath, as usually occurs with a peel, was smooth and discoloration -free-- but I know from my previous experience with this product that my forehead and cheek will eventually peel and reveal dry, irritated, blotchy skin. I will have to spend the next week babying my skin to repair my damaged barrier. I am officially tossing this serum in the trash where it belongs.

Other notes: the smell is vaguely tropical and fairly strong. The texture is very sticky and it does not feel great on the face. Overall, highly displeased with my experience with this serum, and it's especially annoying because it's so costly!

title: A Great Alternative for Acne Prone Tret Lovers!
text:
Let me preface that i was on a high strength prescription retinoid for about a year prior to using this product, so I am an experinced retinol user. What can I say, this is the closest ur gonna get to Retin A results in Canada OTC! I used this product on its own (with moisturizer, a bit of HA, and sunscreen of course) for about two months and it kept my raging hormonal acne at bay, kept my skin smooth, kept my skin tone relatively even, and eve. helped a bit with acne marks too (I've got richly melanated skin). Of course, this isn't the same or as effective as tret, or my holy grail, tazarotene, but its close, and really helped to manage my hormomal acne. I'm also pretty acid averse, and never use acids as they've always irritated my skin, so retinoids are my first line of defense for my highly sentitive, acne prone, oily skin. This product did not irritate my skin (coming from someone with really sensitive skin; can'teven use SA), and I only experinced mild dryness (could also be that I used it in a dry winter climate). I would defo recommend this product for acne prone skin, and don't listen to the haters, start slow, do as much as your skin can handle (I got to the point I was using it every other day to daily just fine), and MOISTURIZE. Listen, most people reach for SA and other acids, not knowing that retinoids work deeper and are much more effective (according to my personal experince and my derms opinion). Don't knock it til you try it, I found my fav acne product. And if you're reading about those who got irritated, remember, this is for experinced retinoid users only.

Side note: I got an extra tube for my mum, 50+ mature dry skin, and also an experinced retinoid user. She loved it too, almost more than her high end stuff!

title: Works great but there’s a knack to using it
text: I used this spf for about a year along with a full Dr. Sturm skincare routine. It was effective, and I learned there is a knack to applying it to avoiding the pilling noted by other reviewers: your skin needs to be really hydrated. I found that when my skin was on the drier side, sun drops were really hard to apply. The product pilled and just wouldn’t sink in. But when my skin was hydrated and supple, it sunk right in and meshed beautifully with my skincare and under makeup. On the one hand, I liked realizing how much more hydrated my skin needed to be…on the other, our skin goes through phases and we doing want something as important and routine as our daily spf to be difficult to apply. Another trick when it did pill (which is something I do for any product that won’t sink in Shaun) is to spray a facial mist over the skin and then massage everything in. Works every time! There’s that hydration factor again I guess. Lastly: be aware that the regulations surrounding skincare filters are different in the US than in Europe, and the formulation for this spf is different here in the states. Sturm products are made in Germany, and my guess is they haven’t just perfected the formula for the US version. In summary, if your skin is generally well hydrated and especially if you have a Sturm routine, I think these drops are great because they can blend so beautifully and look very dewy on the skin. But there are so many amazing spf’s these days where you may get more bang for your buck. And since getting pregnant and now breastfeeding, I can’t even use this one anymore and have switched to mineral sunscreens by Tatcha and Odacité which both perform beautifully.

text:
This is definitely a, "I never write reviews, but I had to for this one" review. 

I'd been wanting to add a retinol into my skincare routine but I was nervous to try one because I have such sensitive skin. Addressing the "pilling" comments - yes that happens but I adjusted how I apply my products an it's fine. You just need to wait a bit. So I put this on first, right after I wash my face. Then you do something else and give your skin time to soak in. I usually brush my teeth or put on my body lotion. Then you add your face cream but instead of rubbing it in your kinda pat it on your face then press it into your skin. Do something else, let it soak in. Then i'll finish with my face oil, and again pat it in don't rub. You'll be fine, no pilling!

title: Fantastic for my oily, acne-prone, dehydrated skin
text:
I have oily, dehydrated, acne prone skin and finding an SPF that doesn't exacerbate at least one of those issues has been challenging. I've been using Star Seed for a week and it's really working for me so I hope this review is helpful for people whose skin is as finicky as mine!

Pros:
- Not dewy or greasy, and doesn't get oily throughout the day
- Absorbs fully into the skin without leaving a film
- Dries down to a lovely velvet-matte finish without drying out my skin
- The tint completely blends in without being too dark or leaving a white cast. That said, I'm super fair so YMMV
- No pilling over skincare or under makeup
- Silicone-free
- It has a slightly tacky finish that my foundation (also silicone free) really grips on to and it stays in place throughout the day, so this seems to double as a primer for me
- It's not hydrating enough by itself at the moment, but I can see how I might be able to skip moisturizer if I use this during the summer
- NO BREAKOUTS!!!!

Cons:
- It's only SPF 30, and my biggest complaint is that it isn't higher. That said, you can use enough product to reach that level of protection and it all absorbs beautifully
- Contains added fragrance. My skin isn't sensitive to fragrance and the scent isn't strong enough to bother me so that's not a dealbreaker for me
- It has butyloctyl salicylate so it's technically not 100% mineral, but again, not a dealbreaker for me personally

I may end up reaching for a product with a higher SPF come summer, but for now it's fantastic and I am SO glad I found it!

title: Good for one stage of the flare-up, not the other.
text: This balm is really good for the initial stages of eczema: when you first have a flare-up and your skin is red and puffy and itchy and life is just awful.  Applied at that stage, it relieves the redness and the itch within about fifteen minutes and continued application makes the irritation go away quickly.  Where it fails, though, is the following stage when the skin is flaky and scaly.  This balm dries it out even more, instead of moisturizers to bring the skin back to normal.  So overall yes, I would 120% recommend this for the initial stages of the eczema flare-up but would suggest going with something different if you’re at the scaly stage.  To add more clarity, I use this to treat flare-ups on my eyes, both underneath and on the lid, and it’s non-irritating for this sensitive area.

title: Moisturizing, high-coverage, broad protection SPF
text:
TL;DR: Love the high coverage (SPF 50), broad-spectrum sunscreen in this not-too-thin-nor-too-thick, moisturizing, clear, subtly-strawberry-scented lip balm that wears comfortably and leaves a soft sheen to the lips.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Medium consistency - has a balm-like quality that feels nourishing without feeling heavy or too thick
* Applies smoothly 
* Wears comfortably on lips; not sticky or tacky
* Moisturizing
* Absorbs easily
* Leaves a soft sheen to lips
* Wears well on own or with a lip liner
* Contains sunscreen
* Love the high SPF & broad-spectrum protection - UVA & UVB protection
* Contains some fabulously nourishing ingredients, including hyaluronic acid, squalane & shea butter
* Expiration date is included on the product (see below)

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* Would be nice to include a Period After Opening (PAO) date on the product (see below) as well as the expiration date that is already included
* Would be nice to have a spot to write down the date you open it, similar to how some Korean skincare / sunscreens do
* $12 seems a little steep for a lip balm but given the high & broad spectrum SPF and excellent hydrating & moisturizing ingredients, there's value in this lip balm
 
FYI:
* Flat tip, slanted applicator
* Has a very subtle strawberry scent when applied but dissipates fairly quickly/doesn't linger very long
* I've taken this on 2 tropical vacations in 2 years, both to humid climates & it's held up well
* Great for travel or use for outdoor activities - sports, hikes, long walks, etc. - the high SPF and broad spectrum protection is a huge plus!
* It started having a chemical/soured scent (that caused me a headache (and I rarely get headaches), about 20 months after opening. I had a few uses left so I pushed through but if I wasn't so close to being done, I would have tossed it.

BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ or BYE-BYE 👋🏼?:
* A definite BUY 🛍️

title: Unfortunately not a favorite of mine
text:
I recently felt that I needed a new addition to my skincare routine and I thought that a new cleanser that supported my barrier would be the best option because my skin barrier can be a bit finicky at times. I have heard great things about this cleanser from Reddit and some influencers so I decided to give it a try and found no ingredients that could potentially trigger and sort of reaction. 

For background on my skin, I have combination, acne prone, dehydrated skin that can suffer from fungal acne from time to time depending on ingredients in products. I bought and returned this cleanser twice and unfortunately both times it did not work out for my skin. The first time I used this product I suffered a reaction and my skin broke out in texture so I returned it. I believe in second chances and I was testing out different skincare products at the time so I decided to give it another go when my barrier was back to normal. The second time wasn’t any better, I broke out in texture (skin like bumps) and I developed acne. So unfortunately it didn’t work out for me :( which was a shame because I really hoped it would. 

This is just my personal skin though I just wanted to put that out there but for the overall cleanser I thought it was a decent options for those who might lean more oily. As I said before, I have combination skin, the first time I tried it I was more oily and I found it to be gentle and slightly hydrating, the second time I tried it my skin was drier and I found it to actually be more stripping than anything. However I did like the texture of the cleanser and the creamy lather. I also didn’t have problems with the product leaking. If you have skin that is dehydrated and leans dry you might want to look for another cleanser. Someone with oiler skin might enjoy this though!

title: Justice for Kosas BB Burst!
text:
I was driven to write this review because this is not something I would have purchased if I was shopping online due to how poorly it’s rated. Which is a shame, because I bought it in stores and absolutely love this product. But because it has such a unique formulation, I can understand how it might catch some people off guard if they’re expecting a more traditional tinted moisturizer. Yes, when it is dispensed out of the container it looks separated…. But that’s by design and it’s because the foundation element is suspended with the skincare actives. Think of it like mixing in moisturizer to your foundation to thin it out, but prepackaged. 

My preferred method of application: I will usually work the product between my fingers/hands in order to warm it up and allow the product’s elements to meld nicely before applying directly to my face. I will occasionally fix any streakiness with a wet beauty blender or brush, but tapping the skin with my fingers works just as well in my opinion. 

For context, I was a long time fan of the MAC face and body sheer foundation and have been looking for something to replace it since it was discontinued/removed from stores. This product has a lot of the same qualities I loved about that foundation: it’s sheer but buildable, dewey but not too oily, layers beautifully with other products and does not cause breakouts on my sensitive/acne prone skin. That formula also really benefitted from being warmed in your hands before applying to the face, so maybe that’s why I like this so much :)

title: Luxe SPF with a smoothe, creamy consistency
text:
TL;DR: Lightweight, mineral sunscreen with a golden yellow tint & a smooth, creamy consistency that feels lightly hydrating and moisturizing on the skin. Depending on skin type & tone, it adds a healthy glow and warmth to the complexion.

Best suited for normal or dry skin types, and possibly combination skin. Those with very oily skin may find the glow to be too much.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Lightweight, silky, soft cream consistency - it literally glides onto the skin
* Mineral UV filters - 20% zinc oxide (the tint to this keeps it from leaving a white cast)
* Contains vitamin C, which gives a soft, natural glow to the skin
* Contains hydrating, moisturizing, & soothing ingredients
* Diminishes appearance of redness & dark spots - it won’t make them completely disappear but just one layer will make them less visible
* Wears well under makeup, no pilling
* Expiration date is listed on back of tube

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* Would be nice if it was packaged in such a way that the user can see how much product remains
* Would love to see a mini version be made available, or even in a discovery set. Or, alternatively, for a deluxe size sample as a promo gwp. It's an expensive sunscreen & being able to try it out beforehand would be great.

FYI:
* Has a soft, fresh, citrusy scent, not overpowering.
* Feels lightly moisturizing & hydrating on my skin but not so much that I would skip my moisturizer
* The tint on this is probably best suited for light-to-medium warm tones
* The glow from this SPF may be too much for those with oily to very oily skin
* Dispenses smoothly from the tube (took 17 pumps on 1st use to get the product to come out)
* Pricey for SPF. I picked it up during Sephora's 50% off sale on certain products.

BUY, BUY, BUY🛍️ or BYE-BYE👋🏼?:
* While the yellow tint isn’t the best match, I do enjoy the feel of this sunscreen. It’s a BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ for me, but when it’s on sale.

TL;DR: Light, thin, tinted mineral sunscreen with hydrating & anti-aging properties. Blends easily, wears well under makeup, evens skin tone & leaves a natural finish. Suitable for all but very dry skin types. Tint better suited to warm, medium toned skin.

title: A must have until I stop breaking out
text:
TL;DR: Thin hydrocolloid patches (with salicylic acid) that suck the gunk out of pimples. A must have in the battle against blemishes. 

WHAT I LIKE: 
* Thin - thinnest pimple patches I’ve used
* Good staying power - stays in place, even overnight (but see below)
* Practically invisible - great for daytime  (but see below)
* These do an amazing job of drawing out all the gunk & pus from a zit (but see below) 
* Can reduce size & redness/inflammation from pimple 
* Speeds up healing process 
* Includes 2 different sized patches
* Good price - the least expensive patches, other than ones from Korean brands

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT: 
* None, really. These are my go-to pimple patches. 
* If I were to be nit picky, I’d suggest having a value sized option available; maybe double the patches. 

FYI: 
* Comes with 22 patches affixed to a sheet & packaged in a sealed pouch inside the box 
* These are meant to be used on pimples that have come to the surface, the head is visible, and there is fluid present. 
* Recommended wear time is 6-12 hours, or overnight
* As the pus is drawn out, it will show through the clear material as a white spot. May need to swap out patch throughout the day. 
* Very thin; may be helpful to use tweezers to remove the patches.
* Not waterproof; slightly water resistant. I did a test by keeping it on in the shower & having the water come down directly onto it; the edges curled up - some patches held on barely; others fell off
* Contains salicylic acid in addition to hydrocolloid (and other ingredients) so if you’re allergic / sensitive, you’ll want to use a different pimple patch. 
* I’ve tried several pimple patches like these - CosRX, Cureology, Hero, Peace Out, Peach Slices, Starface - and these are the best I’ve used. ⭐️

BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ or BYE-BYE 👋🏼?: 
* These are must haves for me. Unless something even better comes along, I’ll be BUYing these for as long as I experience breakouts. 🛍️

title: It's a love hate, but love mostly wins.
text:
I have very dry lips that become extremely dry in colder months.  I'm on a mission to try all lip oils and balms to find the most soothing for me.  This is not in contention for the best, but it is definitely a good option.

The pros - it soothes and hydrates my dry lips.  The effect was almost immediate in softening parts of my lips that felt ready to crack and bleed.  The applicator is plush to make application gentle on sore lips and it adds the faintest hint of red.

The cons - it feels more like a jelly going on than an oil.  It's thick and spreads quickly beyond the lip line.  That's okay, mostly, for me since hydration matters more than looks, but it feels messy.  Probably looks it too, which is why I immediately put this on my nightstand to go with my lip masks.  It doesn't have a taste, but I feel like there is a scent to it that I don't love.  The jelly texture does melt to more of an oil feel, but even as dry as my lips are, it seems to take quite a while to absorb and I'm not the biggest fan of the texture.  My lips aren't sticky, they're slick.  I honestly wiped it off the first time I tried it when the feeling of something oily on my lips persisted for more than 10 minutes.  The first wear was during the day, so I didn't like it, but I tolerate that kind of thing better at night for bed.  I've used this under lip masks after giving it several minutes to settle before layering more on and I've used it on top of lip balms I sometimes apply before bed.  Neither method seems to change the texture on the lip, but both do help soothe and soften my lips at the end of the day to give me a fresh start in the morning.

The price is overall good in comparison to others I've tried with similar effect, so I put it in my 4 star grouping despite the cons.  It also gets a bump in tier for the soothing quality that helped me after mistakingly putting on a plumping gloss that had my lips burning.  This helped with that too.

Maybe the 5% difference in the AHA is really ‘that’ important but I noticed the tiny bumps around my bottom lip and chin area returned when I switched from Ordinary to Paula’s Choice. Just the same as I noticed my skin was seeming uneven and my pores were visible after switching from Ordinary’s toner to Paula’s Choice. I also started to get random pimples which is something I’d usually see a few times a year since using the AHA/BHA peel (~3yrs).

title: Day 1 and Day 30 Review
text:
This product was sent to me for review, with the request that I incorporate it into my routine for 30 days. To maintain consistency, I used both an oil cleanser and a water-based cleanser when wearing makeup or sunscreen; otherwise, I used only the water-based cleanser, followed by the Mineral Milk.
My primary skin concerns are active acne and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, particularly around my t-zone, which tends to experience the most congestion and breakouts. I would self-classify my skin as mild/moderate for blemishes and inflammation so although my skin is not perfect I felt that I would likely get results relatively quickly since I only had a blemish on one side of my jaw and side of my temple on Day 1. I was hopeful that consistent use of the Mineral Milk would help clarify this area and prevent any additional acne however, over the four-week period, I didn’t notice significant changes in my skin’s condition. 

Redness and hyperpigmentation around my nose and chin remained consistent, while my forehead continued to fluctuate with bumps and acne. For active breakouts, I typically apply pimple patches to prevent picking or touching. While using the Mineral Milk, I followed this same approach, but the product’s slow dry-down time made it difficult to apply the patches immediately. I often had to wait over two hours or apply a smaller amount of product to the area before using a patch. Despite the initial dry down time being longer than many of my other products, I did not experience transfer on my pillowcase or additional oiliness on the surface of my skin in the morning that made me feel like I needed to rinse my face. Other people have commented on the scent, I also mutually agree that it has a very niche smell from the actives which does not dissipate on the skin quickly after application so if you are sensitive to fragrances it would be something to take in consideration but I accustomed to it quickly personally.

title: I have been really enjoying this lip mask!
text:
I was surprised to read the negative reviews of this lip mask, because I personally really like it. I wanted to leave a review with my own thoughts, so that people could get a different perspective. To be clear, I'm not saying that those who disliked this product are wrong or that you shouldn't listen to them, I just wanted to share my own, very different experience. You can read all the reviews, both positive and negative, and decide for yourself whether this lip mask is right for you.
I have been using this lip mask pretty much every day for a couple of weeks now, and here are my thoughts:
- it does smell nice, similar to a caramel Macchiato. I will say that I get more caramel than coffee from it, but I do get a bit of both. The scent is there, but not overly strong or overpowering. 
- I personally have not noticed any plastic, perfume-y, or otherwise unpleasant taste (unlike some flavored squeeze tube lip balms I've tried). However, other reviews do mention this, so YMMV.
- more importantly to me at least, this lip mask does what it's supposed to do and leaves my lips moisturized, soft and smooth. It is very comfortable when on, and stays on all night without drying out.
- it is not sticky, gritty, or grainy (like some other lip masks I've tried).
- in addition to using it as an overnight lip mask, I find it also works great as a daytime lip balm. It's perfect for cold and dry fall/winter weather! 
- I appreciate that it comes in a tube rather than a little pot, so I don't have to use my fingers to apply it and make a mess. The applicator tip is comfortable as well.
- you can't beat the price!
- overall, I have no complaints about this product. I find it to be both effective as a lip mask, and enjoyable to use. It is one of my favorite lip masks I've tried so far. I am glad I bought it, and plan to get a few more during the sale when they're 30% off.

title: Amazing serum for crepey skin w/ loss of firmness
text: This serum is very light and silky, and absorbs into my skin quickly. I don’t use a body moisturizer over this even though that’s recommended (I’m such a rebel!) because I don’t want to dilute the amazing ingredients in this product. I haven’t encountered any dryness, and I actually find using this serum alone provides moisture. I’m on my second bottle, and I’m very happy with the results! I’m naturally pretty thin, but my skin has started to look crepey in areas and there is some loss of firmness. I apply this to my chest, stomach, bum, and armpit area… I saw a photo of myself and was horrified when I noticed the wrinkly skin in front of my armpits. I don’t have much fat on my stomach but, thanks to being preggo a decade ago and genetics, the skin on my abdomen has lost firmness and has lines and a crepey texture. title: Fantastic, affordable moisturizer!
text:
As someone who’s always on the lookout for an effective, no-nonsense moisturizer that supports the skin barrier without causing breakouts or irritation, The Ordinary's Natural Moisturizing Factors + PhytoCeramides is a standout.
Texture & Application:
This moisturizer has a lightweight yet creamy texture that absorbs easily without leaving a greasy or sticky residue. It spreads effortlessly and layers well under sunscreen or makeup, making it ideal for both day and night routines. A little goes a long way, so the tube lasts longer than you'd expect.
Key Ingredients & Benefits:
What sets this formula apart from the original NMF moisturizer is the inclusion of phyto-ceramides—plant-derived lipids that help restore and strengthen the skin barrier. Combined with amino acids, fatty acids, urea, and hyaluronic acid, it effectively locks in hydration and supports long-term skin health. The formulation is fragrance-free, making it a great choice for sensitive or reactive skin types.
Performance:
After consistent use, skin feels smoother, more resilient, and well-hydrated. It’s especially beneficial for anyone dealing with dryness, flakiness, or barrier impairment. I noticed reduced redness and less tightness in dry areas within a few days. It also pairs well with active ingredients like retinoids or acids without pilling or irritation.
Downsides:
While it's a strong performer, it may not be rich enough on its own for those with very dry skin or during harsh winter months. In that case, layering it with a facial oil or occlusive balm may be necessary. Also, those with oily skin might find it slightly too rich for daytime use in humid climates.
Final Thoughts:
This is a thoughtfully formulated, affordable moisturizer that punches above its price point. It’s a great daily hydrator for anyone looking to support their skin barrier with minimal filler ingredients.

Once a week for 2 weeks at night after my shower, I left it on for 2 hours ( so it can really work before diluting it with oil ) before applying 100% Squalene Oil from Biossance and I let the oil to absorb in for 1 hour before going to  sleep.

My skin was now ready for the Dr Dennis Gross 0.5% retinol pads. I followed the same schedule with 0.5% as i did with 0.2% retinol pads.

I only wish they would have much bigger packaging for the 0.5% retinol pads. ( for every night for a whole year )
I don't understand why they are sold out at Sephora for such a very long time, because they are available on Dr Dennis Gross website, but unfortunately they don't ship internationally.

text:
I rarely write reviews on makeup/skin products, but THIS product has earned my undying loyalty. Although this product has lasted me forever, I live in fear of it being discontinued or something and have an actual stockpile. For reference, I am in my mid-thirties and my lips are naturally large and pigmented, which WOULD be a blessing, but until this product, what usually happened is my lips would dry out quickly and they would crack to the point of bleeding. I wouldn’t be able to wear lip products because my lip texture was so uneven and anything with alcohol (lip stains) would sting the cracked, dry lips, it was a nightmare. I had tried everything, including Vaseline (everyone used to swear it would work) the Laniege (I may have spells that wrong) lip mask (which I had been assured at the time was the best), but everything disappointed.

Enter my Fenty holy grail! This is the only product that has EVER worked on my lips. The packaging is unique and LASTS FOREVER. A small amount goes a long way. The balm is soothing, it doesn’t have a taste or scent that throws me off, and you can tell it works because YOU STILL FEEL IT THE NEXT MORNING! 

I never used to be able to wear lip products, but my cracking is so much better. This product has healed my lips and makes them not only look better, but feel better. I would pay 4x the price, but the price is EXTREMELY REASONABLE FOR WHAT IS OFFERED. This product is underrated, and more people should know how important this is!

title: Lazy girl body care star (be careful in winter!)
text:
I have about 1/6 of the jar left so I finally feel like I can write a well-informed review.

I really like this product because it’s super easy to use, the jar is actually quite travel friendly, it’s very moisturizing, and the scent is nice and mild. It also sinks into the skin rather quickly, so by the time I’m out of the shower and drying off I don’t feel like I have a layer of grease sitting on top of my skin.

For context, one of my main reasons to purchase this was because I recently started accutane and my skin was feeling (and looking) painfully dry. I’m also very lazy/super tired in the evening. I know a multi-step body moisturizing routine would really benefit me, but some days I just want to be done once I leave the shower. This shower salve definitely hits all the marks, being super convenient and super hydrating. I love using it after shaving (I wouldn’t say it prevents ingrown hairs but I’ve found it helps) and it always leaves my skin nice and soft.

The only issue I’ve ever had with the product was when I was keeping it in my gym bag in the winter. While I recommend using it at the gym be careful of the temperature where you store it. It was fairly cold and basically froze solid. I could scrape layers off to use, but it was TOUGH. Do not attempt to use your nails—you will break them. That being said, in the summer and spring (and some of the fall) it returned to a good temperature and as far as I can tell the formula wasn’t altered by the temperature changes.

If you have dedicated body care routine I don’t know if you need this. But if you’d like to shorten/simplify or just want something easy and that provides excellent hydration for rather minimal effort, I really recommend this!

title: Everything I Wanted: Sans Moisture?
text:
Ingredient-wise, this looked like everything I wanted: beta glucan, NMFs, urea, etc. Texture-wise, it’s a refreshing gel that feels nice at first with no excess shine. But minutes later, the hydration vanishes. My skin feels dry, almost as if I never applied anything. So when does “lightweight” become too lightweight? :? 

I tried all the tricks in my arsenal: layering hydrating toners, applying on damp/dry skin (even semi-damp/dry skin) misting thermal water on top. Alas, same result every time: all gel, no moisture. Since I’m beyond the return day window, I’ve been trying to use it up by adding some drops of facial oil or mixing with another moisturizer, however, that defeats the purpose of using this as a stand-alone moisturizer.

Is it awful? Not really. If you’re truly oily, this could work, especially in summer or the for those in disbelief of using a moisturizer due to having oily skin. But for most skin types, it’s too bare-bones, and could pill and/or cause breakouts from some of the lipid components.

I think The Ordinary could really improve this by reformulating. Right now, it’s basically a water gel with a sprinkle of NMFs, leaving it tacky in both texture and value. By adding more glycerin, ceramides, and NMFs, this could become a proper water gel-cream. Even 5% urea would give it a boost, and the product could then compete with more expensive brands, like SkinFix, Tatcha, or Prequel!

Overall, I had high hopes but was let down. Fingers crossed they revisit and relaunch this one with a better formula. *And yes, I’ve tried and know about The Ordinary's other moisturizers...Don’t come at me, ya’ll.

title: Vanilla + Juniper Icing
text:
Vanilla Vibezzz, full size.

I've tried this twice in the little sample form that Sephora gives out before buying the large size. I think it's wise as it isn't a scent for everyone.
Firstly, scents SMELL different ON different people because they mix with your body chemistry and heat. I always recommend trying a sample before buying a large size.
SECONDLY, this isn't a plain gourmand vanilla. A lot of people complain that this isn't giving "vanilla vibes". It's because it's not ONLY vanilla. It contains Juniper Berries- one of my favorite berries. Now, juniper berries are NOT going to be like a nice sweet blueberry. Juniper berries are used a lot in cooking, not baking.
What are juniper berries scent notes? Here ya go: Fresh & Crisp: The dominant note is a fresh, invigorating scent, like a cool breeze brushing past pine trees. Piney & Woody: It features a clear coniferous aroma, reminiscent of pine or cedarwood. Spicy & Peppery: There are warm, earthy, and sometimes peppery spicy undertones. Resinous & Sweet: You can detect a faint sweetness, a resinous quality, and subtle floral or herbal notes as the scent develops. 
Mix that with the vanilla. You get this scent.To me it smells like vanilla icing and juniper Berries- slightly peppery, slightly herbaceous. I love it for when I want a "vanilla AND" scent. If I want just a gourmand vanilla, I reach for something else.
My skin type is dry, sensitive, with eczema. I find this does not irritate my skin- but always test things out yourself. It does not absorb easily into my skin and I will stay "oily" for a while. I put it on, let it sit tight, and then go change into my clothes for the day. 
PROS: skin is shiny, looks healthy, smells good
CONS: skin acts like I put oil on it, have to be careful before touching things

title: Rouge Member saying GOODBYE Sephora!
text:
I’ve been a Sephora Rouge member for years, spending thousands annually and holding a Sephora credit card. That ends now.

I purchased the Patrick Ta Major Glow High Shine Body Lotion from Sephora’s website. The marketing promised a “skin-perfecting high shine” and showed comparison photos with dramatic glow versus no shine. Over a weekend, my two daughters and I tested it side-by-side with a Trader Joe’s lotion that cost a fraction of the price — and the Trader Joe’s lotion outperformed this $55 “luxury” product.

We used about 50% of the bottle during testing — enough to give it a fair shot over two days. I returned it to Sephora’s Las Vegas distribution center, expecting them to stand by their well-advertised return policy. Instead, I was told my return was denied for “excessive use” and I would not be refunded. They didn’t even offer to send the product back.

I spoke to two customer service representatives and a supervisor named Akuinda. All three refused to help, citing “policy” and making it clear there was no flexibility — not even for a Rouge member who has spent thousands with the company.

So let’s be clear: Sephora now has both my money and the product. Rouge members, take note — their return policy clearly isn’t what it’s marketed to be.

If this is how Sephora is going to treat its most loyal customers, I’ll be taking my business elsewhere, closing my Sephora credit card, and sharing my experience widely. Keeping both the refund and the product isn’t customer service — it’s theft.

title: A life savor
text:
Shocked by some of the other reviews and photos. I am on my third purchase of this eye cream and have never had an issue with the packaging. 

I started using this eye cream in 2019 in a sample I received and made my first purchase in 2020. At the start of the pandemic I started noticing fine lines around my eyes. I was 26 at the time and feeling a bit self-conscious. I also contemplated getting botox just to stop these lines from getting worse. With the pandemic in full swing, I decided to try out all the products in this Kate Somerville line and it totally changed my skin. The serum and moisturizer have dramatically my skin and stopped all of my adult acne. I haven't had anything more than small clogged pores since I used this product line. As for this eye cream, my fine lines went away for good. These products help keep my skin cells turning over and my eyes look brighter than ever.

If this will be your first time using a retinol product, expect to purge. My skin purge lasted about two months. For the eye cream, this meant that my eye area was a bit sensitive temporarily and I had to use a lot of SPF more than normal. I made the mistake of using this eye cream the night before I went on a hike, which was a bad idea. My eyes were bright red for about another day. Now that I am way past my purge, this is not an issue for me at all. I use a regular amount of SPF and never have any burning, redness, or flaky skin. It's important to remember that this happens with all retinol products - you have to trust the process and give it about 3 months to work. 

I am probably on the younger side of the spectrum of people buying this product, so I'm sure results will vary, but this was a life saver for me. Now that I'm just a smidge older, I'm glad I didn't spend the money on botox, which probably would have messed up my face in my long term at this age.

title: Vanilla + Juniper Icing
text:
Vanilla Vibezzz, full size.

I've tried this twice in the little sample form that Sephora gives out before buying the large size. I think it's wise as it isn't a scent for everyone.
Firstly, scents SMELL different ON different people because they mix with your body chemistry and heat. I always recommend trying a sample before buying a large size.
SECONDLY, this isn't a plain gourmand vanilla. A lot of people complain that this isn't giving "vanilla vibes". It's because it's not ONLY vanilla. It contains Juniper Berries- one of my favorite berries. Now, juniper berries are NOT going to be like a nice sweet blueberry. Juniper berries are used a lot in cooking, not baking.
What are juniper berries scent notes? Here ya go: Fresh & Crisp: The dominant note is a fresh, invigorating scent, like a cool breeze brushing past pine trees. Piney & Woody: It features a clear coniferous aroma, reminiscent of pine or cedarwood. Spicy & Peppery: There are warm, earthy, and sometimes peppery spicy undertones. Resinous & Sweet: You can detect a faint sweetness, a resinous quality, and subtle floral or herbal notes as the scent develops. 
Mix that with the vanilla. You get this scent.To me it smells like vanilla icing and juniper Berries- slightly peppery, slightly herbaceous. I love it for when I want a "vanilla AND" scent. If I want just a gourmand vanilla, I reach for something else.
My skin type is dry, sensitive, with eczema. I find this does not irritate my skin- but always test things out yourself. It does not absorb easily into my skin and I will stay "oily" for a while. I put it on, let it sit tight, and then go change into my clothes for the day. 
PROS: skin is shiny, looks healthy, smells good
CONS: skin acts like I put oil on it, have to be careful before touching things

title: Just Okay
text:
I recently purchased the Laura Mercier Tinted Moisturizer with Sunscreen in hopes of simplifying my morning routine. I was using both a separate moisturizer and sunscreen and thought this product could combine the benefits of both into one step. Unfortunately, it didn’t quite live up to that expectation.

On the first day, I applied it without any moisturizer underneath, and my skin looked chalky, dry, and even a bit flaky. It emphasized texture in a way I didn’t expect. The next day, I applied my regular moisturizer before using the tinted sunscreen, and it went on much more smoothly and looked significantly better. So while it has some hydrating qualities, it definitely doesn’t replace a standalone moisturizer—at least not for my skin.

Another downside is how it wears throughout the day. I work long hours, and by the end of the day, my skin tends to look more oily than dewy. It's not terrible, but it does leave me feeling like I need to blot or touch up more than I’d like.

On the positive side, I haven’t experienced any breakouts from this product, which is always a concern for me. Also, I ordered the shade online and was pleasantly surprised that it matched my skin tone really well. That part was a win.

Overall, it’s an okay product. It has its pros, but I don't think it’s the all-in-one solution I was hoping for. I’ll likely keep using it for now, but I’m also keeping an eye out for other options that might better suit my needs.
